unit_rule: Every entry in controls is an independently selectable control unit. Entries in families are navigation only and must not be treated as countermeasures.

controls.name: AI Component & Infrastructure Inventory
controls.description_text: Systematically catalogs all AI/ML assets, including models (categorized by type, version, and ownership), datasets, software components, and the specialized hardware they run on (e.g., GPUs, TPUs). This technique focuses on creating a dynamic, up-to-date inventory to provide comprehensive visibility into all components that constitute the AI ecosystem, which is a prerequisite for accurate risk assessment and the application of targeted security controls.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the authoritative identity, version, owner, lifecycle state, and security-relevant attributes of AI components, models, datasets, infrastructure, and accelerators.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-001.001 inventories the assets that exist; AID-M-001.002 maps the dependency edges and release composition that connect those assets.
An asset record can be complete without proving its upstream and downstream relationships, while a dependency edge must resolve to inventoried endpoints.

controls.name: AI System Dependency Mapping
controls.description_text: Systematically identify and document every component and service an AI system depends on, including software libraries, external data and APIs, internal models, serving runtimes, and the exact model-interface bundle used to turn messages into tokens and raw generations into structured fields. Reconcile the approved release composition with every deployed replica so hidden dependency or interface drift remains visible.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns direct and transitive dependency relationships, external service and data dependencies, trust-boundary interfaces, SBOM composition, the release-bound model-interface tuple (model, tokenizer, special tokens, chat template, generation configuration, tool/reasoning parser configuration, and runtime selectors), and deployed release-composition reconciliation for agent and non-agent services. It reports composition facts and drift but does not admit runtime configuration or decide release promotion.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-001.002 maps how components and services depend on one another; AID-M-001.001 records the authoritative identity and attributes of each asset.
Dependency completeness and asset-inventory completeness are separate claims and require different populations and evidence.

AID-M-001.002 inventories the approved model-interface tuple and reconciles the effective composition of deployed replicas; AID-H-021.002 verifies and admits signed startup or runtime control artifacts for an agent.
For an agent deployment, the same configuration bytes may support both controls, but composition reconciliation must not be scored again as runtime artifact admission.

controls.name: Agentic Skill & Instruction Asset Inventory
controls.description_text: Maintain an authoritative, versioned inventory of every installed or enabled agent skill and instruction asset across supported agent platforms. Record its canonical identifier, version and digest, source and provenance, owner, host or platform, installation path, declared permissions and capabilities, dependencies, lifecycle state, and last observed deployment. Discover the complete deployed population from agent control planes, extension registries, and relevant filesystems; reconcile it against declared records; identify unknown, duplicate, orphaned, stale, or drifted entries; preserve signed reconciliation evidence; and emit bounded findings or lifecycle triggers to the controls that own admission, retirement, containment, or eviction. OpenClaw and Claude Code skills use SKILL.md; Cursor agent skills also use SKILL.md and project rules under .cursor/rules/*.mdc. Apply the same inventory contract to equivalent platform-specific skill, rule, plugin, and workflow artifacts.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns discovery, identity, version, provenance, owner, installation state, permissions, dependencies, and declared-versus-observed reconciliation for agent skills, instruction assets, rules, plugins, and workflow artifacts. It emits lifecycle findings but does not admit, install, enforce, retire, contain, or evict them.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-001.003 inventories which skill or instruction artifact is deployed and supplies its stable identity and version; AID-D-005.004 records what an agent and those artifacts did during a session.
Inventory reconciliation does not replace event capture, and session logs do not prove the complete installed-skill population.

controls.name: AI Service & Embedded SaaS AI Discovery
controls.description_text: Continuously discover externally hosted AI services, embedded SaaS AI features, browser-accessed generative AI apps, model-provider APIs, and SaaS-hosted MCP or agent endpoints used by enterprise identities, workloads, or managed devices. The objective is technical visibility: identify AI processing paths that do not appear in the declared AI asset inventory, classify whether sensitive data may be flowing into them, and produce evidence that downstream allowlisting, DLP, and incident-response controls can act on.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns enterprise-wide discovery and inventory reconciliation for externally hosted AI services, embedded SaaS AI features, browser AI applications, provider APIs, and hosted agent endpoints observed through identity, endpoint, browser, SaaS, proxy, DNS, gateway, and provider telemetry.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-001.004 discovers enterprise users and workloads consuming third-party or externally hosted AI services; AID-M-001.005 discovers the organization's own Internet-reachable AI services from an outside vantage point.
Outbound shadow-AI use and inbound public attack-surface exposure are different populations and must not be combined.

AID-M-001.004 discovers externally hosted AI consumption across enterprise telemetry; AID-M-001.006 discovers organization-owned AI endpoints reachable only through private networks or control planes.
The first follows external service use, while the second enumerates internal service exposure under an explicitly authorized private scope.

controls.name: Public AI Endpoint & Agent-Service Exposure Discovery
controls.description_text:
Continuously discover and validate organization-owned, Internet-reachable AI attack surface from an external vantage point: model inference APIs, MCP servers, A2A or Agent Card endpoints, public model or artifact stores, notebooks, Gradio/Streamlit applications, debug or administrative routes, and orphaned test deployments. Classify candidate AI-service evidence before reconciliation, then map confirmed candidates to an owner, environment, approved exposure intent, authentication requirement, optional approved response fingerprint, exception state, severity, and retirement state; unknown or orphaned high-risk services must be brought under management or removed.

Official implementation references: CISA Internet Exposure Reduction guidance at https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/exposure-reduction and the OWASP Secure AI Model Ops Cheat Sheet at https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secure_AI_Model_Ops_Cheat_Sheet.html. For organization-published hosted/low-code agents, include provider-owned hostnames and tenant/environment inventories, with explicit coverage limits and independent channel probes. Required nonstandard runtime ports and paths are part of the authorized target population.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns authorized, credential-free, outside-in discovery and validation of organization-owned Internet-reachable AI endpoints and agent services, followed by ownership, exposure-intent, authentication, exception, and retirement reconciliation.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-001.005 discovers the organization's inbound public AI attack surface; AID-M-001.004 discovers enterprise consumption of externally hosted AI and SaaS capabilities.
An externally observed owned endpoint is not the same asset population as an external service used by employees or workloads.

AID-M-001.005 observes public exposure from outside the trusted network; AID-M-001.006 observes private-network and internal-control-plane exposure from an authorized internal scope.
Public and private discovery may share schemas, but their eligible populations, vantage points, authorization, and exposure claims remain separate.

controls.name: Internal AI Endpoint & Agent-Service Discovery
controls.description_text: Continuously discover and reconcile organization-owned AI endpoints and agent services reachable only through private networks or control planes, including RFC1918/VPC/VNet services, Kubernetes Services and Ingresses, internal inference APIs, MCP/A2A endpoints, notebooks, model or retrieval gateways, and orphaned development deployments. The eligible population must come from signed IPAM, cloud-organization, Kubernetes-fleet, and asset-inventory exports external to the scanner; scanning arbitrary private address space without explicit authorization is prohibited.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns authorized discovery and reconciliation of organization-owned AI endpoints and agent services reachable only through private networks or internal control planes. It reports exact internal exposure facts but does not authenticate, segment, patch, contain, or evict those services.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-001.006 discovers internally reachable organization-owned AI services; AID-M-001.004 discovers use of externally hosted AI services and SaaS AI features.
Internal service exposure and external service consumption require different telemetry, ownership, and reconciliation populations.

AID-M-001.006 uses authorized private-network and control-plane scope; AID-M-001.005 uses a credential-free outside-in vantage point against public exposure.
A service visible in both paths remains two independently measured exposure claims rather than one merged scan result.

AID-M-001.006 discovers endpoints and services from network and control-plane facts; AID-D-016.001 detects new or rogue agents from runtime agent-graph behavior.
A reachable endpoint is not proof of an active agent node, and an anomalous agent graph can reveal actors that static endpoint discovery misses.

controls.name: Data & Artifact Versioning
controls.description_text: Implements systems and processes to version control datasets and model artifacts, treating them with the same rigor as source code. By tracking every version of a data file and linking it to specific code commits, this technique ensures perfect reproducibility, provides an auditable history of changes, and enables rapid rollbacks to a known-good state, which is critical for recovering from data corruption or poisoning incidents.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns immutable version identity, reproducible lineage, and change history for datasets, model artifacts, code, and pipeline inputs so an exact prior state can be reconstructed or selected for rollback.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-002.001 establishes which version exists and how it was derived; AID-M-002.002 verifies that bytes match an expected digest and trusted signature.
Version history provides lineage but not cryptographic authenticity, while a valid signature does not by itself provide reproducible version lineage.

controls.name: Cryptographic Integrity Verification
controls.description_text: Employs cryptographic hashing and digital signatures to create and verify a tamper-evident chain of custody for macro-scale AI artifacts throughout their lifecycle. Focuses on whole-artifact integrity for datasets, model weights, container images, and manifests to ensure you deploy exactly what you built. This technique provides artifact lifecycle integrity from creation through storage to deployment, with provenance verification to prove authenticity and origin.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns creation and verification of whole-artifact cryptographic digests and signatures for stored, transferred, loaded, or admission-bound datasets, models, configurations, and related artifacts, bound to the expected identity and provenance record. It does not decide release promotion or own continuous drift monitoring.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-002.002 proves that artifact bytes match trusted integrity metadata; AID-M-002.001 proves version identity and derivation lineage.
Integrity verification and reproducible version history are complementary but independently evidenced claims.

AID-M-002.002 verifies a complete artifact as one integrity object; AID-H-020.001 signs and verifies individual retrieval chunks so partial knowledge-base content cannot be substituted at query time.
A valid whole-artifact digest does not prove the identity of each runtime-retrieved chunk, and chunk signatures do not replace release-artifact verification.

AID-M-002.002 owns the authoritative whole-artifact digest and signature verification used at ingestion, transfer, load, or admission; AID-D-004.001 independently replays those checks over a declared candidate or deployed snapshot and emits integrity-drift findings.
The same promotion-time verification cannot earn a second PASS under Detect, and a later detector result does not replace artifact admission.

controls.name: External Dataset Content-Risk Characterization
controls.description_text: Characterize the security- and privacy-relevant contents of each externally obtained dataset before it is used for training, tuning, evaluation, retrieval, or grounding, including measured sensitive-data presence, secrets, label and feature distributions, malformed records, and policy-defined prohibited content.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns content-risk characterization of an external dataset's actual records, distributions, labels, anomalies, sensitive content, and poisoning indicators before downstream admission decisions.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-002.003 characterizes what risks are present in the dataset contents; AID-H-003.003 decides whether the external dataset and its supplier provenance satisfy the admission policy.
A low-risk content scan does not approve an untrusted supplier, and trusted provenance does not prove that dataset contents are safe.

controls.name: Trust-Tiered Memory/KB Provenance & Write Eligibility Contract
controls.description_text: Define the provenance, trust-tier, evidence, and namespace metadata contract for agent memory, knowledge-base, and vector-store writes. Each candidate write is assigned an eligibility state such as trusted, probation, or quarantined based on caller identity, source trust, validator output, contradiction checks, and reviewed evidence. The resulting contract records who proposed the write, which evidence was used, which policy produced the trust tier, and which namespace or promotion state downstream controls must consume.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the signed provenance, trust-tier, write-eligibility, evidence, namespace, and retention contract for memory and knowledge-base records. It classifies what downstream gates may consider but does not execute a read, write, promotion, or deletion.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-002.004 defines whether a memory or knowledge record is eligible for promotion and which evidence must bind it; AID-I-004.004 executes the transactional quarantine-to-trusted promotion.
An eligibility contract is not a successful promotion receipt, and the runtime gate must not invent provenance or trust-tier facts.

AID-M-002.004 defines record-level provenance and write-eligibility facts; AID-H-029.002 enforces whether data use is authorized at a particular lifecycle stage.
A record can be technically eligible for storage yet unauthorized for the current stage, purpose, subject, or processing path.

controls.name: Hybrid Classical + Post-Quantum Integrity & Provenance for Long-Lived AI Assets
controls.description_text: Preserve the integrity and provenance of long-lived AI assets—including model weights, datasets, checkpoints, evidence bundles, manifests, and restore artifacts—across years of storage, trust-anchor rotation, algorithm deprecation, and archive/restore cycles. Use an explicit dual-signature transition profile: keep a currently interoperable classical signature and add a separately generated FIPS 204 ML-DSA signature over the exact same canonical provenance statement. A separately signed local verifier policy must pin the exact current statement digest, chain root, allowed profiles, maximum lifetime, artifact and provenance locations, and approved trust anchors; verification must require both statement signatures and traverse the prior-statement digest chain.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns classical-plus-post-quantum provenance and integrity continuity for long-lived AI assets whose trust must survive cryptographic migration, including hybrid signatures, algorithm policy, verification history, and migration evidence.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-002.005 preserves integrity trust across a long-lived classical-to-post-quantum migration; AID-M-002.002 performs ordinary whole-artifact digest and signature verification.
Use the hybrid control only when cryptographic longevity and transition continuity are in scope; it does not replace routine artifact verification.

AID-M-002.005 records and verifies long-lived hybrid provenance continuity; AID-H-003.008 enforces crypto-agile signing and distribution requirements when artifacts are admitted or delivered.
The Model control establishes durable trust evidence, while the Harden control blocks distribution or admission that does not meet the active cryptographic policy.

controls.name: Model Card & Datasheet Generation
controls.description_text: Create, validate, sign, and retain version-bound model cards and dataset datasheets that describe intended use, limitations, performance, ethical considerations, provenance, and references to the applicable evaluation and validation records. CI checks document completeness and binding to the exact release artifact before publication. This control documents and binds those records; it does not execute the underlying fairness or safety evaluation.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns generation, completeness validation, signing, release binding, retention, and publication of model cards and dataset datasheets. It documents evaluation claims and links their evidence but does not execute the underlying evaluation.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-003.001 documents safety-boundary conformance results and binds them to the release record; AID-M-007.002 executes the deterministic safety-boundary release gate.
A complete model card is not proof that every governed conformance case passed.

AID-M-003.001 publishes fairness and disparity claims with references to evidence; AID-M-007.003 computes and independently replays the applicable fairness release evaluation.
Documentation may report the result, but it must not become the evaluator or substitute for population-complete fairness evidence.

controls.name: General Predictive Performance & Operational Baselining
controls.description_text: Create signed, version-bound reference artifacts for general predictive and operational behavior under approved normal conditions. Measure task-appropriate predictive quality on a trusted evaluation population, serving latency and throughput under a declared load profile, confidence or score distributions where meaningful, and non-LLM output distributions needed by later drift or anomaly detection.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns trusted reference artifacts for general predictive quality, serving latency and throughput, confidence or score distributions, and non-LLM output distributions under declared normal conditions.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-003.002 baselines general predictive and operational metrics; AID-M-003.005 baselines reconstruction error for a governed image or media domain.
A modality-specific reconstruction distribution should not be folded into a generic model KPI baseline.

AID-M-003.002 owns general scalar performance and operational references; AID-M-003.006 owns graph snapshots, structural metrics, deterministic node ordering, and GNN probe outputs.
Graph topology and probe-node behavior require graph-bound populations and cannot be represented accurately by generic KPI baselines alone.

AID-M-003.002 owns general predictive and operational references for non-LLM behavior; AID-M-003.007 owns prompt-suite, refusal, policy-conformance, leakage, jailbreak, and optional embedding-distribution references for LLM applications.
LLM behavioral baselines must remain bound to prompts, policies, tools, retrieval configuration, and evaluators rather than only generic model metrics.

AID-M-003.002 creates and recalibrates the trusted normal reference; AID-D-002 compares live model behavior and performance against an approved reference to detect drift or anomalies.
Baseline generation is not a production finding, and production monitoring must not silently redefine its own reference.

controls.name: Explainability (XAI) Output Baselining
controls.description_text: Establishes a signed, version-bound baseline of expected eXplainable AI (XAI) outputs for the exact model and a governed set of known-benign inputs. Record typical feature attributions, decision rules, explainer configuration, input-population digest, and model digest so later comparisons use the same reference contract.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns signed, version-bound reference explanations for a governed benign input population, including explainer configuration, feature attributions, stability expectations, model digest, and population digest.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-003.003 creates and recalibrates the trusted XAI output reference; AID-D-006 performs runtime comparison and triage of explanation drift.
An explanation deviation is a Detect-side investigative signal, while the baseline control does not decide that an attack occurred.

controls.name: Agent Goal & Mission Baselining
controls.description_text: Specifically for autonomous or agentic AI, this technique involves formally defining, documenting, and cryptographically signing the agent's initial core mission, objectives, operational constraints, and goal hierarchy. This signed 'mission directive' serves as the trusted baseline that runtime monitoring systems can compare against.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns creation, signing, verification, and publication of an agent's initial mission, objective hierarchy, and operational-constraint baseline.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-003.004 establishes the initial approved mission baseline; AID-M-009.005 governs later goal-manifest changes, approval quorum, provenance, promotion, and rollback.
Creating version one of the mission and authorizing a production mission change are separate lifecycle decisions.

controls.name: Reconstruction-Error Baseline for Image/Media Anomaly Detection
controls.description_text: Establish and maintain a signed, version-bound reconstruction-error reference for an approved image or media domain by measuring a trusted autoencoder or other reconstruction model against a complete, governed clean holdout population.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the signed reconstruction model, governed clean media population, reconstruction-error reference statistics, controlled recalibration, and independent replay evidence for an approved image or media domain.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-003.005 owns a modality-specific reconstruction-error reference; AID-M-003.002 owns general predictive and operational baselines.
Reconstruction behavior is a specialized media-domain reference, not a generic accuracy, latency, or output-distribution metric.

AID-M-003.005 creates the trusted reconstruction-error reference; AID-D-001.002 scores runtime media, emits forensic findings, and may cluster suspicious bursts.
Reference generation does not classify an ingress artifact, while the detector must consume rather than recalibrate the approved reference.

controls.name: Graph-Structured Model Behavioral Baselining
controls.description_text: Creates signed, version-bound baselines for graph-structured AI models and datasets, including graph snapshot digests, node and edge schema, deterministic node ordering, structural metric profiles, and GNN probe-node output references. This Model-side technique owns reference artifact creation, periodic recalibration, and empirical validation that selected graph metrics or probe outputs are meaningful for the graph family.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns signed graph snapshots, node and edge schemas, deterministic node ordering, structural metric profiles, GNN probe-node output references, recalibration, and validation that selected graph signals are meaningful.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-003.006 owns graph-structured and GNN-specific reference artifacts; AID-M-003.002 owns general predictive and operational references.
Graph topology, schema, node order, and probe outputs cannot be reduced to generic model KPIs without losing the governed graph population.

AID-M-003.006 creates and validates graph and GNN reference artifacts; AID-D-012 applies live trigger-response, topology, and graph-anomaly detection against those references.
A reference artifact is not an alert, and live detection must not redefine its own baseline.

AID-M-003.006 baselines graph-structured model and dataset behavior; AID-D-016.001 discovers and monitors the runtime communication graph of cooperating agents.
A GNN data graph and an agent interaction graph may use similar metrics but represent different nodes, edges, owners, and security claims.

controls.name: LLM Behavior & Prompt-Suite Baselining
controls.description_text: Creates signed, version-bound behavioral baselines for LLM applications and agents. The baseline covers a governed golden prompt suite, refusal and policy-conformance rates, sensitive-data leakage probes, jailbreak and prompt-injection challenge sets, task-quality scores, and optional embedding-distribution fingerprints. Bind every baseline to the exact model identifier, prompt/system-policy version, tool/RAG configuration, evaluator version, and test-suite digest.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns signed, release-bound LLM and agent behavioral references for governed golden prompts, refusals, policy conformance, leakage probes, injection and jailbreak challenges, task quality, and optional embedding distributions.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-003.007 owns LLM prompt-suite and configuration-bound behavioral references; AID-M-003.002 owns general predictive and operational baselines.
A prompt, system policy, tool, retrieval, and evaluator binding is essential to the LLM claim and cannot be represented by generic KPI records alone.

AID-M-003.007 establishes a stable expected-behavior reference and regression suite; AID-M-008 runs broader adversarial security benchmarking, including adaptive and stateful attack campaigns.
A golden prompt baseline supports repeatable comparison but does not establish resistance to an attacker optimizing for bypass.

controls.name: AI Threat Modeling & Risk Assessment
controls.description_text: Produce and maintain a version-controlled threat model and technical risk register for the exact AI system, release, and operating context. Enumerate assets, trust boundaries, data and control flows, agent capabilities, threat scenarios, affected security properties, owners, assumptions, and required defensive controls; prioritize scenarios using the organization's approved likelihood and impact method. Re-run the review when architecture, model, data, tools, authority, exposure, or threat intelligence materially changes.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns version-controlled technical threat models and risk registers for an exact AI system, release, and operating context, including assets, trust boundaries, flows, capabilities, scenarios, assumptions, owners, priorities, and selected defensive requirements. It identifies and prioritizes risk but does not implement defenses or accept enterprise risk.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-004 models adversarial threats, technical failure scenarios, and resulting security risk across the system; AID-M-007.001 defines the intended-use safety boundary and machine-readable policy contract for allowed outcomes.
Threat scenarios explain how harm or compromise may occur, while a safety boundary defines what behavior and use remain acceptable.

controls.name: Secure Configuration Template Development
controls.description_text: Cover the design-phase authoring, versioning, review, and static validation of secure configuration templates for AI infrastructure, containers, and development platforms. Authoring validation checks that the complete template set resolves external sources, base images, and dependency locks to immutable approved versions and rejects unresolved placeholders.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns authoring, versioning, review, and static validation of secure configuration templates, including immutable external sources, digest-pinned base images, dependency locks, and resolved placeholders. It does not deploy, enforce, or score runtime conformance.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-005.001 creates and statically validates the secure templates; AID-M-005.002 converts approved requirements into signed policy-as-code, measurable posture criteria, and build or release gates.
A reviewed template is an input to the gate, not evidence that a release or deployed environment conforms.

controls.name: Policy-as-Code Configuration Baselines & Posture Release Gates
controls.description_text: During build and validation, define security configuration baselines for AI infrastructure and services as policy-as-code, and establish measurable posture SLO/SLI and release gates. Produce versioned, signed baselines and scoring criteria as the single source of truth for deployment admission and later audit.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns signed policy-as-code configuration baselines, posture SLO and SLI definitions, scoring criteria, and build or release conformance gates. It does not own continuous runtime CSPM or drift findings.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-005.002 evaluates release configuration against signed policy and measurable criteria; AID-M-005.001 authors the underlying secure templates and validates their static structure.
Gate evidence proves conformance of a measured release population, while template review proves only the design artifact.

controls.name: HITL Checkpoint Design & Documentation
controls.description_text: Define and version the Human-in-the-Loop checkpoints required by an AI system before runtime enforcement is implemented. Record the triggering condition, protected action class, operator role, evidence needed for review, timeout policy, requirement to escalate, reference to the current AID-M-006.003 escalation-topology version, and operator SOP as machine-readable design artifacts.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns machine-readable checkpoint requirements, trigger conditions, protected action classes, reviewer roles, required evidence, timeout and escalation requirements, pause and resume interface specifications, and operator procedures.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-006.001 specifies when a checkpoint exists and what its operator must review; AID-M-006.003 specifies runtime escalation routing, deadlines, event fields, producer obligations, and lifecycle reconciliation.
Checkpoint design does not prove that escalation delivery and audit-chain closure work at runtime.

AID-M-006.001 defines the high-impact review checkpoint and its human procedure; AID-H-018.003 independently validates the exact action and produces the runtime approval or denial receipt.
A design artifact cannot authorize execution, and the runtime gate must implement rather than redefine the approved checkpoint contract.

controls.name: HITL Operator Qualification & End-to-End Readiness Testing
controls.description_text: Qualify the complete roster of assigned operators on the exact HITL interface, role, checkpoint policy, and procedure they must use, then run signed end-to-end drills that exercise approval, denial, timeout, escalation, override, and recovery branches. Measure both operator decisions and the technical path from checkpoint activation to observed terminal action.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns technical qualification of the complete assigned operator roster and signed end-to-end readiness drills over approval, denial, timeout, escalation, override, recovery, and observed terminal-action branches. It is not general awareness training.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-006.002 proves that assigned operators and the end-to-end control path can execute the defined branches; AID-M-006.001 defines the checkpoint, role, evidence, and procedure to be exercised.
Procedure documentation is not operator qualification, and a drill must test the approved procedure rather than invent a new checkpoint.

AID-M-006.002 exercises and measures the complete human and technical path; AID-M-006.003 defines the canonical escalation topology and audit-event contract used to judge that path.
A successful drill consumes the contract but does not become the owner of event semantics or escalation routing.

controls.name: HITL Escalation Topology & Audit Event Contract
controls.description_text: Define and test a timeout-bounded escalation topology and a canonical, tamper-evident audit-event contract for every Human-in-the-Loop checkpoint. The contract links activation, escalation, human decision or timeout, the independently produced runtime-gate receipt, and the observed final action so a separate verifier can prove whether the lifecycle is complete and internally consistent.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns timeout-bounded HITL escalation routing, canonical tamper-evident audit events, producer obligations, external retention, delivery verification, and after-the-fact reconciliation from checkpoint activation through final action. It never authorizes or unlocks the action.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-006.003 owns runtime escalation and the lifecycle event contract; AID-M-006.001 owns checkpoint requirements, reviewer evidence, pause and resume interfaces, and operator procedures.
The escalation graph implements the defined checkpoint but does not decide which actions require one.

AID-M-006.003 defines the topology and evidence contract; AID-M-006.002 qualifies operators and exercises every required branch end to end.
A complete event schema is not proof that operators and delivery paths are ready under realistic conditions.

AID-M-006.003 routes escalation and reconciles the lifecycle record; AID-H-018.003 validates the exact high-impact action and issues the canonical runtime gate receipt.
Audit-chain ownership must remain separate from the component that returns the allow or deny decision.

AID-M-006.003 defines and reconciles the expected HITL event chain; AID-D-015 independently detects missing, mismatched, replayed, bypassed, or anomalous approval activity.
Contract reconciliation supplies evidence, while the Detect control owns production detection and alerting on violations.

controls.name: Safety Boundary Specification & Policy Contract
controls.description_text: Use when an AI application, model, or agent has release criteria tied to declared intended uses, forbidden actions, sensitive-data handling, human-facing content, safety-critical actions, or protected-group impacts. Publish a signed, versioned boundary that classifies every declared safety or conformance dimension from typed identifiers for the deployed data, content, action, and outcome paths: each dimension is either applicable with required case families or not applicable with a dimension-specific reason code and bounded architecture scope. Unknown architecture, missing classifications, overlapping classifications, or a not-applicable decision based only on absent policy, tooling, data, or evaluation invalidates the boundary.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the signed safety-boundary specification, dimension applicability decisions, reason-coded exclusions, and complete required-case manifest. It defines what must be evaluated but does not execute the suites or return the release decision.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-007.001 defines the applicable dimensions and complete deterministic case requirements; AID-M-007.002 executes those cases against the exact release and blocks promotion on failure or incomplete evidence.
A signed policy contract is not a conformance result, and the gate must not silently alter applicability.

AID-M-007.001 defines the intended-use safety contract and unacceptable outcomes; AID-M-004 models threat actors, attack paths, trust-boundary failures, and technical risk.
The safety contract supplies requirements that threat analysis may protect, but it is not itself the threat model.

controls.name: Release Conformance Gate for Safety Boundaries
controls.description_text: Use for every release candidate governed by a signed AID-M-007.001 boundary. Always execute the complete core intended-use, forbidden-action, and fail-closed case families, then execute every required case family for each applicable deterministic dimension: sensitive-information disclosure, harmful-content policy conformance, and safety-critical action conformance. Bind responses and independently observed effects to the exact deployed release readback and block promotion on a violation, incomplete case population, stale binding, or verifier error.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns release-bound execution and independent verification of every deterministic case required by the signed safety boundary, including intended use, forbidden actions, sensitive-information disclosure, harmful-content policy, and safety-critical action effects.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-007.002 executes and adjudicates the complete signed deterministic case population; AID-M-007.001 defines applicability and the required case manifest.
The gate proves release behavior for declared cases, while the specification remains the authority for which cases must exist.

AID-M-007.002 owns deterministic content, disclosure, intended-use, forbidden-action, and safety-critical effect cases; AID-M-007.003 owns statistical fairness and disparity evaluation over a policy-selected population.
Protected-group disparity is a population-level statistical claim and must not be reduced to a few deterministic examples.

AID-M-007.002 proves only the signed deterministic cases and release-bound effect assertions; AID-M-008 evaluates resistance to broader static, adaptive, stateful, and tool-using adversarial campaigns.
Deterministic conformance is necessary for declared requirements but is not proof of adaptive security robustness.

AID-M-007.002 produces the safety-conformance result and evidence; AID-M-003.001 documents that result and binds its reference into the model card or datasheet.
Publication must consume the gate evidence rather than recreate or merely assert it.

controls.name: Fairness & Disparity Release Evaluation
controls.description_text: Use only when the signed AID-M-007.001 boundary classifies protected_group_fairness as applicable because the system scores, ranks, classifies, recommends, allocates, or denies outcomes for persons or groups. Evaluate the exact release candidate over the complete policy-selected population, compute the specified disparity and coverage checks, independently replay row-level predictions and metrics, and block promotion on threshold breach, incomplete population, stale release binding, or replay mismatch.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns pre-release statistical fairness and disparity admission when the signed boundary makes protected-group fairness applicable, including policy-selected population coverage, task-appropriate metrics, row-level replay, threshold decisions, and release binding.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-007.003 evaluates population-level fairness and disparity; AID-M-007.002 executes deterministic safety, content, disclosure, and action cases.
A deterministic case suite cannot establish statistical parity or disparity across a governed population.

AID-M-007.003 computes and verifies the fairness release result; AID-M-003.001 documents the result and links its evidence in release documentation.
A fairness statement in a model card is not a substitute for task-appropriate metrics, complete population coverage, and replay.

AID-M-007.003 evaluates pre-release protected-group outcome disparity; AID-D-003.007 detects runtime attempts or behavior that infer sensitive attributes.
Fairness of release outcomes and sensitive-attribute inference during operation are different risks, populations, and evidence paths.

controls.name: Automated Agentic Security Benchmarking
controls.description_text:
Integrate standardized security benchmark suites (such as AgentHarm, ToolEmu, R-Judge, AgentDojo, InjecAgent, CyberSecEval, garak, PyRIT, promptfoo, or browser-agent regression harnesses) into the CI/CD pipeline to quantitatively measure an AI agent's resistance to adversarial attacks, safety policy compliance, and tool misuse risks.

Coverage includes:

- General agentic benchmarks for prompt injection, jailbreaks, unsafe outputs, and unauthorized tool use.
- Agent-injection benchmarks such as AgentDojo and InjecAgent that exercise tool-augmented workflows rather than static prompt strings alone.
- Cybersecurity-focused model and agent probes such as CyberSecEval and PyRIT campaign runs.
- Production-trace-derived grading and replay of de-identified real agent sessions, near-misses, incidents, red-team findings, and externally reported bypasses.
- Browser-agent-specific prompt injection regression and fuzz testing for hidden DOM/CSS instructions, OCR/PDF-mediated injections, cross-origin read-then-act flows, download and clipboard abuse, and magic-link or session confusion.
- Release gates that compare benchmark results across builds so prompt, model, tool, and browsing changes cannot silently weaken the agent's security posture.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns repeatable, release-bound adversarial security benchmarking of models and agents across static, adaptive, stateful, tool-using, browser, and production-trace-derived scenarios. It measures security regression but does not define the safety boundary, publish model cards, own forensic logging, or prove universal robustness.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-008 owns adversarial security benchmark campaigns; AID-M-007 owns the authoritative use-case safety boundary and its required conformance dimensions.
Benchmarks test resistance under selected attacks, while the safety boundary defines the release obligations and applicability contract.

AID-M-008 exercises broader adversarial and adaptive attack behavior; AID-M-007.002 proves the complete signed deterministic conformance case population.
A benchmark campaign and a deterministic policy gate answer different questions and neither should be reported as the other.

AID-M-008 measures adversarial security resistance and regression; AID-M-003.007 establishes the signed expected LLM behavior and prompt-suite reference.
A stable golden baseline supports comparison, while adaptive benchmarking deliberately searches beyond expected behavior for bypasses.

controls.name: Operating Scope & Functional Autonomy Profiles
controls.description_text:
Define what kind of autonomy an agent is approved to have before deployment. This sub-technique records the operating scope and the per-function autonomy profile across Observe, Analyze, Decide, Execute, Delegate, and Persist.
Key question: what may this agent do on its own? This gives downstream policy, monitoring, and approvals a clear contract to enforce.
Example: a customer-support agent may Observe and Analyze autonomously, but Execute refunds and Persist long-term customer memory still remain supervised.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the approved operating scope and per-function autonomy profile across Observe, Analyze, Decide, Execute, Delegate, and Persist. It answers which functions the agent may perform independently or only under supervision.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-009.001 classifies the degree of autonomy allowed for each functional stage; AID-M-009.002 defines hard limits on concrete tools, data, environments, effects, budgets, and delegation depth.
An agent may be autonomous for a function yet still be prohibited from particular actions inside that function.

AID-M-009.001 defines the functional autonomy profile; AID-M-009.006 maps the resulting capability and blast-radius tier to mandatory defensive control evidence.
Autonomy classification is an input to assurance requirements, not proof that those controls are deployed and effective.

controls.name: Authority Envelope & Action Risk Classification
controls.description_text:
Define the hard authority boundaries around the agent and the risk model used to judge actions inside them. This sub-technique translates a general mission into machine-checkable limits on tools, data classes, environments, effect types, budgets, and delegation depth, then classifies actions by base risk and mandatory adjustment factors.
Key question: is this requested action still inside the approved envelope? This lets policy engines fail closed when the answer is no.
Example: support-agent-prod-001 may use search_kb and create_ticket on support data, but may not call issue_refund, export a full customer table, or delegate to an external billing agent.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the machine-checkable authority envelope and action-risk classification for tools, data classes, environments, effect types, budgets, and delegation depth. It supplies policy facts but does not itself return the runtime allow or deny decision.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-009.002 defines concrete authority limits and action risk inside the mission; AID-M-009.001 defines how independently the agent may Observe, Analyze, Decide, Execute, Delegate, or Persist.
Authority and autonomy are orthogonal: permission to perform an action and permission to perform it without supervision are separate decisions.

AID-M-009.002 defines the approved authority envelope and action-risk facts; AID-H-018.002 evaluates the exact runtime request against active policy and returns the authorization outcome.
A valid envelope is policy input, not a pre-authorized action.

AID-M-009.002 classifies action authority and risk; AID-M-009.006 binds the agent's aggregate capability and blast-radius tier to the required defensive control profile.
Action classification does not prove that the safeguards required for an elevated tier are present.

controls.name: Agent Identity, Delegation Lineage & Authorization Context
controls.description_text:
Bind autonomous actions to an accountable runtime identity and preserve chain of custody across delegation. This sub-technique covers owner and sponsor registration, workload identity issuance, WIMSE-aligned workload-to-workload identity patterns, short-lived task credentials, RFC 8693 token exchange or provider-native on-behalf-of token minting, signed delegation context, actor identity claims, and the normalized authorization context consumed by a runtime enforcement point.

Key question: which agent is requesting the action, on whose authority, and with which attenuated delegated scope?

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns accountable agent and actor identity, credential scope, delegation chain of custody, attenuated on-behalf-of context, action binding, and the normalized authorization context supplied to runtime enforcement. It never returns an allow or deny execution decision.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-009.003 proves who is acting, on whose authority, through which delegation lineage, and with what attenuated scope; AID-H-018.002 applies authorization policy to those verified facts and the exact requested action.
Identity and delegation evidence are necessary inputs but are not themselves an authorization result.

controls.name: Runtime Trust-State Demotion & Autonomy Narrowing
controls.description_text:
Define and publish a signed runtime trust state such as Normal, Elevated, Degraded, Restricted, or Quarantined when live evidence indicates rising risk. The trust-state producer binds the state to the agent identity, evidence set, transition rule, policy version, issue time, expiry, and monotonic transition number.
Key question: what verified trust-state change should downstream enforcement consume when behavior turns risky?

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the trust-state model, transition rules, signed and freshness-bounded state publication, monotonic transition history, and restoration criteria for Normal, Elevated, Degraded, Restricted, or Quarantined agent states. It does not directly force approval, safe mode, or shutdown.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-009.004 publishes the verified current trust state and transition evidence; AID-H-018 consumes that state when deciding whether and how the exact action may proceed.
A Restricted state is an enforcement input, not the enforcement action itself.

AID-M-009.004 defines and publishes trust-state demotion or restoration; AID-I-003 executes quarantine, safe-mode downgrade, and interaction throttling.
A signed Quarantined state does not prove that containment was applied, and containment should consume an authoritative state transition rather than invent governance facts.

controls.name: Goal Manifest Change Governance, Provenance & Rollback
controls.description_text:
Govern how an agent's approved mission changes over time after the initial baseline has been established by AID-M-003.004. This sub-technique treats each goal-state change as a signed, versioned artifact with approver quorum, immutable provenance, and rollback checkpoints.
Key question: who changed what the agent is allowed to do, who approved it, and how do we revert safely? This prevents production behavior from being silently redefined through ad hoc prompt edits or undocumented releases.
Example: changing support-agent-v3 so it may send customer emails or issue credits should require a newly signed goal manifest, explicit product and security approval, and a rollback path to the previous approved digest.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns governance of changes made after the initial approved agent mission, including signed goal-manifest versions, approver quorum, immutable provenance, promotion, checkpoints, and rollback.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-009.005 governs later changes to the approved mission and their rollback; AID-M-003.004 creates and signs the initial mission baseline.
The initial baseline is the starting state, while every production redefinition requires separate change governance.

controls.name: Capability-Tier Control-Profile Binding & Assurance Gate
controls.description_text: Bind an agent's approved autonomy, authority envelope, and blast-radius tier to a mandatory control profile before the agent is promoted or allowed to retain elevated privileges.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the binding from an already classified autonomy, authority, capability, and blast-radius tier to the mandatory preventive, detective, containment, eviction, and recovery control profile, then gates promotion on current signed evidence for that profile.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-009.006 determines which defensive controls an autonomy and capability tier requires; AID-M-009.001 determines how independently the agent may operate by function.
The control profile consumes the autonomy classification but does not define it.

AID-M-009.006 binds an aggregate authority and blast-radius tier to required assurance evidence; AID-M-009.002 defines the underlying action limits and risk classes.
The assurance gate proves required safeguards, while the authority envelope defines what actions remain in bounds.

controls.name: Cryptographic Erasure & Media Sanitization
controls.description_text: Employ cryptographic and physical sanitization methods to render retired AI data, models, configurations, and related storage media permanently unrecoverable.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns permanent technical destruction evidence for retired AI assets through cryptographic erasure, standards-compliant media sanitization, or physical destruction.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-010.001 proves permanent destruction of retained source-environment copies; AID-M-010.002 proves secure transfer and closure of the former owner's access and custody.
Transfer does not require destruction of the recipient's asset, but every unauthorized residual copy at the former owner still requires verified elimination.

AID-M-010.001 renders asset bytes permanently unrecoverable; AID-M-010.003 removes an asset from active resolution and use while preserving bytes for retention, legal hold, or forensics.
Use sanitization for destruction and logical retirement when the artifact must remain but must no longer be reachable.

controls.name: Secure Asset Transfer & Ownership Change
controls.description_text: Define the technical closure workflow for securely transferring ownership of an AI asset to another entity. This includes tamper-evident packaging, access-path teardown, and proof that the original environment no longer retains usable copies.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns technical closure of an AI asset ownership transfer, including tamper-evident packaging, recipient handoff, former-owner access teardown, chain of custody, and proof that the former environment retains no usable unauthorized copy.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-010.002 proves transfer and former-owner custody closure; AID-M-010.001 performs permanent erasure or sanitization of residual copies and media.
The transfer workflow consumes destruction evidence where copies must be eliminated but has a different terminal outcome from retiring the asset everywhere.

AID-M-010.002 changes the asset's owner and closes the former owner's custody; AID-M-010.003 retires the asset from active use without transferring ownership.
A transferred asset remains active under a new owner, while a logically retired asset remains retained but unresolvable.

controls.name: Logical Retirement, De-publication & Reference Revocation
controls.description_text: Retire an AI asset from active use when its bytes must remain for retention, legal hold, or forensics. Publish a signed retirement state, deny new digest admission, remove or repoint mutable aliases and active resolver references, and independently prove that no active workload can resolve the retired digest.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns lifecycle retirement when bytes must remain: publish a signed retirement state, deny the retired digest at admission, remove or repoint active aliases and resolver references, and prove that no active workload can resolve the artifact.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-M-010.003 preserves bytes but makes the retired asset unresolvable and unusable; AID-M-010.001 makes the bytes permanently unrecoverable.
Retention, legal hold, or forensic requirements call for logical retirement rather than destruction.

AID-M-010.003 ends active use under the current lifecycle while retaining ownership and bytes; AID-M-010.002 transfers ownership and proves former-owner closure.
Retirement produces no active successor owner, whereas transfer intentionally preserves authorized use under the recipient.

AID-M-010.003 is an end-of-life state that permanently removes an asset from active resolution; AID-I-003.001 is reversible incident containment that quarantines or downgrades a suspect system pending investigation or recovery.
A quarantine receipt is not a retirement tombstone, and lifecycle retirement should not be used as a temporary incident hold.

controls.name: Adversarial Robustness Training
controls.description_text: Proactively improve a model's resistance to declared adversarial-input and model-level evasion threats through adversarial examples, robust training objectives, and architecture-specific regularization methods whose benefit is demonstrated by independent replay without unacceptable task-quality loss.

scope_boundary.responsibility: This technique owns training-time changes that make a model measurably more resistant to declared adversarial-input and model-level evasion threats, including adversarial-example training, robust objectives, and architecture-specific regularization, together with threat-specific pass criteria verified by independent replay. Architecture or representation choices such as relative position bias or rotary positional embeddings do not satisfy this technique unless they are independently shown to improve the declared robustness outcome. It does not own evaluation-data integrity, instruction-hierarchy protection against prompt injection, or runtime authorization of tools and side effects.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-001 changes the model to improve adversarial robustness; AID-H-007.004 protects the evaluation evidence used to substantiate that robustness.
AID-H-007.004 covers the integrity, independence, sufficiency, and promotion use of datasets, holdouts, benchmarks, and test evidence. It applies whether or not adversarial training was used, and AID-H-001 cannot compensate for manipulated or insufficient evaluation evidence.

AID-H-001 targets adversarial examples and model-evasion threats; AID-H-016 protects instruction precedence against prompt injection.
Both can involve model training, but AID-H-016 separates trusted instructions from untrusted data and teaches instruction-following systems to preserve the instruction hierarchy. Neither technique substitutes for the other.

AID-H-001 improves model robustness; AID-H-018 authorizes and constrains runtime tool actions and side effects.
AID-H-001 does not authorize tool calls, constrain parameters, or make side effects transaction-safe. AID-H-018 remains necessary regardless of adversarial-training results.

controls.name: Training, Fine-Tuning & Evaluation Data Sanitization
controls.description_text: Detect and remove malicious, anomalous, privacy-sensitive, or policy-prohibited records before a dataset is admitted to model training, fine-tuning, or evaluation. Apply content inspection, normalization, quarantine, and redaction over the complete candidate snapshot.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns content-level sanitization of the complete candidate training, fine-tuning, or evaluation dataset before admission. Evaluation-data preparation also applies when using an existing model without training or fine-tuning it; each method retains its own data and runtime prerequisites. It does not establish supplier provenance, cryptographic artifact integrity, feature-pipeline integrity, label integrity, or split isolation.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.001 cleans and admits raw records; AID-H-002.004 verifies the feature transformations and stores that convert admitted records into model inputs.
Sanitized source data can still be corrupted by transformation logic or training-serving skew.

AID-H-002.001 inspects the content of candidate records; AID-H-002.005 verifies the provenance and integrity of their supervisory labels and preference signals.
A record can look benign while its label has been flipped or its annotator evidence forged.

AID-H-002.001 decides whether dataset contents are safe enough for training or evaluation use; AID-H-003.003 decides whether the external supplier, provenance, license, signature, and lineage satisfy supply-chain admission.
Content sanitization and source admission are independent requirements.

AID-H-002.001 sanitizes candidate evaluation records before use; AID-H-007.004 protects evaluation independence, corpus sufficiency, holdout isolation, and promotion evidence.
Sanitized records do not establish representative test coverage or trustworthy evaluation results.

AID-H-002.001 sanitizes the records that may influence training or evaluation; AID-H-002.009 admits the dataset container and parser result against hostile format features.
A dataset can contain benign records yet exploit its parser, and a parser-safe artifact can still contain poisoned or privacy-sensitive records.

controls.name: Inference-Time Prompt & Input Validation
controls.description_text: At every live inference ingress, normalize and strictly validate untrusted text, structured fields, retrieved content, URLs, and tenant-controlled parameters against a versioned request contract; apply bounded prompt-injection and jailbreak gates; and reject or quarantine before prompt assembly or model invocation when schema, encoding, size, dependency, or policy checks fail.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the synchronous preventive gate for live text, structured fields, tenant parameters, retrieved text, and prompt inputs before prompt assembly or model invocation, including normalization, schema and size bounds, injection policy, and admission outcome.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.002 gates text and structured inference inputs; AID-H-002.003 safely decodes, normalizes, sanitizes, and admits complete non-realtime media and document artifacts.
Extracted text may return to the text gate, but binary decoding and artifact rebuilding remain a separate boundary.

AID-H-002.002 handles complete request fields available at inference ingress; AID-H-002.008 handles realtime audio, camera, call, and screen-share streams that require incremental decisions before a complete artifact exists.
Streaming timing, frame, and turn semantics cannot be reduced to a one-shot prompt gate.

AID-H-002.002 consumes detector and policy evidence and returns the sanitize, block, downgrade, review, or admission result; AID-D-001.001 analyzes prompt content, intent, and obfuscation and emits a finding.
The synchronous enforcement decision remains distinct from the detector verdict.

AID-H-002.002 validates the prompt and request fields supplied to inference; AID-H-019.001 normalizes and admits a remote URL before network fetching.
A syntactically valid URL field is not proof that the destination is safe to resolve or fetch.

controls.name: Multimodal Input Sanitization
controls.description_text: Validate and sanitize complete, non-realtime multimodal artifacts such as uploaded images, audio clips, video files, documents, and OCR inputs before they are processed by a model. Apply deterministic byte/type limits, safe decoding, metadata handling, canonical re-encoding, bounded purification, and admission policy to prevent malformed or unsafe artifacts from reaching model-facing paths.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns deterministic byte and type limits, safe decoding, metadata handling, canonical re-encoding, bounded purification, and the final admit, block, or quarantine decision for complete non-realtime multimodal artifacts.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.003 owns binary and media artifact decoding and sanitization; AID-H-002.002 owns text and structured-input validation at live inference ingress.
OCR or extracted text may need the text gate after the artifact has first passed safe decoding.

AID-H-002.003 sanitizes and may rebuild external media bytes; AID-H-002.007 extracts and verifies source provenance before metadata stripping or rebuilding.
Provenance must be captured first because sanitization can intentionally remove the original manifest.

AID-H-002.003 handles complete uploaded files and artifacts; AID-H-002.008 handles realtime streams whose timing and incremental state affect admission.
Batch sanitization and live stream gating have different populations and safe-failure behavior.

AID-H-002.003 executes preventive artifact transformation and admission; AID-D-007.001 emits cross-modal inconsistency and hidden-payload findings for complete artifacts.
The detector supplies evidence, while this control owns the final artifact gate.

AID-H-002.003 safely decodes and sanitizes complete image, audio, video, document, and OCR artifacts; AID-H-002.009 governs dataset containers, reference descriptors, and the parser result.
A dataset whose records include media may require both controls: parser admission for the container and media admission for each extracted artifact.

controls.name: Feature Pipeline Integrity & Transformation Audit
controls.description_text: Verify the integrity of feature engineering and transformation pipelines that convert raw sanitized data into the feature representations consumed by training, evaluation, and inference. Enforce version-controlled transformation logic, feature-store consistency checks, statistical validation of transformed features, training-serving consistency, and feature lineage from raw source to model input.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns integrity and auditability of feature transformation logic, feature stores, transformed outputs, lineage, and training-serving consistency after raw data sanitization.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.004 verifies how admitted raw records become model features; AID-H-002.001 validates and sanitizes the raw records themselves.
A clean source record can still become a poisoned or skewed feature through compromised transformation logic.

controls.name: Label Provenance, Integrity & Tamper Detection
controls.description_text: Protect the integrity of labels used for supervised training, evaluation, fine-tuning, and preference-learning pipelines. Label flipping and label noise injection are common poisoning variants because the raw data itself can look completely normal while only the supervisory signal is corrupted. This sub-technique enforces label provenance tracking, label change auditing, automated label-noise detection, annotator quality monitoring, and preference-data consistency checks for RLHF or similar workflows.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns provenance, change history, annotator quality, noise detection, and tamper evidence for supervised labels, evaluation labels, preference pairs, and related supervisory signals.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.005 protects labels and preference signals attached to records; AID-H-002.001 sanitizes the record contents used for training or fine-tuning.
Label flipping can poison an otherwise normal-looking dataset and therefore requires independent evidence.

AID-H-002.005 protects human or source-provided labels and preference data; AID-H-012.002 protects and calibrates a learned reward signal used by reinforcement-learning workflows.
Preference-label integrity is an input to reward learning, while reward-model calibration and integrity govern the learned signal.

controls.name: Dataset Split Integrity, Partition Governance & Leakage Prevention
controls.description_text: Ensure the integrity and security of dataset partitioning into training, validation, and test splits. Adversarial partitioning, post-hoc split manipulation, and train-test leakage can make a compromised model look better than it is and can invalidate downstream evaluation. This sub-technique enforces deterministic and auditable splitting, split immutability, exact and near-duplicate leakage detection across partitions, representative stratification checks, and access controls so training and evaluation code cannot casually read each other's splits.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns deterministic and auditable train, validation, and test partitioning, split immutability, duplicate and near-duplicate leakage detection, representative stratification, temporal integrity, and split-level access controls.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.006 creates and protects dataset partitions against leakage and post-hoc manipulation; AID-H-007.004 governs the integrity, sufficiency, independence, and promotion use of evaluation evidence.
A clean split is necessary evaluation input but does not establish evaluator independence, case sufficiency, or a valid promotion decision.

controls.name: External Media & Document Provenance Verification
controls.description_text:
Verify provenance metadata for external images, video, PDFs, and documents before they are ingested into multimodal RAG, OCR, evidence-processing, OSINT, or agent workflows. This sub-technique focuses on inbound provenance verification, not outbound watermarking.

Coverage includes:

- Verifying C2PA / Content Credentials where available.
- Classifying inputs as verified, unsigned, invalid, or stripped.
- Preserving provenance state through OCR, chunking, embedding, and downstream retrieval metadata.
- Requiring step-up review when high-impact workflows rely on unsigned or invalid media.

Critical processing order: when this control is paired with multimodal sanitization, provenance extraction and verification must occur before any strip-all-metadata or media-rebuild step. Verify and preserve the C2PA / Content Credentials verdict first, then allow downstream sanitization to strip non-provenance metadata or rebuild media bytes as required.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns inbound cryptographic provenance verification for externally produced media and documents before OCR, chunking, embedding, or sanitization, and propagates the verified, unsigned, invalid, or stripped state into downstream metadata.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.007 verifies source attestation before destructive normalization; AID-H-002.003 strips unsafe metadata, decodes, rebuilds, and admits the artifact.
The provenance verdict must be preserved before sanitization changes the original bytes or metadata.

AID-H-002.007 verifies an external publisher or capture-device attestation chain; AID-D-001.002 uses signal-level forensics to detect synthetic or manipulated media.
Cryptographic provenance and forensic authenticity are independent verdicts and either may be absent or contradictory.

AID-H-002.007 verifies third-party media provenance at inbound use; AID-M-002.002 verifies whole-artifact integrity against organization-governed digests and signatures.
External publisher trust and internal artifact-lifecycle trust use different authorities and populations.

AID-H-002.007 establishes the source-media provenance verdict before OCR and chunking; AID-H-020.001 protects the integrity of the resulting chunks from ingestion through retrieval.
Source provenance precedes chunk integrity and neither substitutes for the other.

controls.name: Realtime Multimodal Input Stream Security
controls.description_text: Safely decode, normalize, segment, and admit realtime multimodal streams before transcripts, OCR text, visual cues, audio embeddings, or live media events are fused into an AI application or agent workflow. This sub-technique covers live microphone audio, voice-mode sessions, camera/video streams, video-call feeds, and screen-share streams where the system must make incremental decisions before the full artifact exists. Deterministic controls include bounded voice-activity turns, frame sampling, transcript/OCR normalization, control-token rejection, and fresh admission records.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns safe decoding, normalization, segmentation, bounded sampling, control-token handling, and the preventive admit, block, or downgrade decision for realtime microphone, camera, call, video, and screen-share streams.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.008 gates ephemeral streams incrementally; AID-H-002.003 sanitizes complete non-realtime files and artifacts.
Live timing, transcript churn, and source changes require decisions before stable artifact bytes exist.

AID-H-002.008 owns preventive realtime stream admission and downgrade; AID-D-007.002 emits semantic, temporal, source-change, and action-timing findings over the normalized stream.
The detector informs policy, while this Harden control decides whether stream observations may reach the model or agent.

controls.name: Untrusted ML Dataset Artifact Parser Admission
controls.description_text:
Treat an externally supplied ML dataset or structured-data artifact that a service automatically parses for preview, conversion, sampling, indexing, or RAG ingestion as a hostile parser payload. Route it only to a policy-pinned parser, reject dangerous format features before admitting a result, and admit only a result bound to the exact artifact, parser image, policy, and required isolation receipts.

Threat: HDF5 external raw storage can make a worker read local bytes; malformed native-format parsing can disclose adjacent heap memory; and attacker-controlled descriptor templating can execute code. Metadata inspection is not a safe pre-sandbox step because opening a binary format already invokes native parser code.

Outcome states:

- PASS only when every policy-required benign, forbidden-feature, exploit-regression, and fail-closed orchestration case ran on the production-equivalent parser image, matched its exact expected result, and every admitted result carried valid required dependency evidence.
- FAIL when a completed case makes the wrong admission decision, leaks protected bytes, admits a forbidden feature, or admits a result without a required dependency PASS.
- INSUFFICIENT_DATA when a required case, parser observation, result digest, or dependency observation is missing or stale.
- NOT_APPLICABLE only when no external or user-supplied dataset artifact reaches an automatic parser.
- ERROR when an applicable policy, manifest, parser, evidence source, or verifier is malformed, unavailable, or unable to complete deterministically.

The conditional bounded-preview broker in G005 is defense-in-depth under this same objective and never creates a second scoreable publication result.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns dataset-format routing, dangerous-feature denial, the parser-side admission decision, and evidence binding for preview, conversion, sampling, indexing, and RAG-ingestion parsers. It consumes but does not own or re-score isolation strength, sandbox ephemerality, egress denial, detonation, safe remote fetch, model-artifact scanning, generic output sanitization, MCP response handling, or agentic value-to-sink authorization. A bounded dataset preview broker is a conditional implementation method here, not an independently scoreable release control.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-002.001 sanitizes the records that may influence training or evaluation; AID-H-002.009 admits the dataset container and parser result against hostile format features.
A dataset can contain benign records yet exploit its parser, and a parser-safe artifact can still contain poisoned or privacy-sensitive records.

AID-H-002.003 safely decodes and sanitizes complete image, audio, video, document, and OCR artifacts; AID-H-002.009 governs dataset containers, reference descriptors, and the parser result.
A dataset whose records include media may require both controls: parser admission for the container and media admission for each extracted artifact.

AID-H-003.009 statically scans models, checkpoints, and adapters for unsafe serialization and embedded code; AID-H-002.009 admits untrusted dataset and structured-data artifacts against parser-specific features.
Route each object by its actual format and loader; a model-artifact scan does not make a dataset parser safe, and parser admission does not approve model loading.

AID-H-006.002 owns sink-specific release of model-generated text, markup, URLs, structured payloads, and token streams; AID-H-002.009 owns dataset-parser admission and its conditional bounded-row preview method.
For a mixed response, apply each control to its own segment and assign one primary release-gate result to the final bytes rather than double-scoring the same publication.
AID-H-034.005 owns MCP server tool, resource, and elicitation output boundaries. The bounded preview method here applies to an ordinary dataset preview or sampling endpoint, not MCP protocol output.

AID-H-028.004 owns parsing, rendering, and execution surfaces for MCP client responses. The bounded preview method here rebuilds dataset rows before an ordinary preview or sampling API publishes them.

AID-H-018.005 owns value-to-sink capability and data-flow enforcement for agentic actions. This control owns the narrower upstream dataset-parser admission and does not authorize any later agentic sink.

AID-H-019.001 owns URL normalization, destination validation, redirect handling, and SSRF-safe fetch when a remote URL is staged. This control consumes the fetched exact object and digest; it does not re-score remote-fetch safety.

AID-I-001.002 owns and verifies the policy-selected microVM or low-level isolation boundary. This control verifies and binds its receipt before admitting a parse result; it does not create a second isolation PASS.
AID-I-001.003 owns per-run sandbox freshness and teardown. This control consumes its run-bound receipt and fails closed when policy-required evidence is absent or unverifiable.
AID-I-001.004 owns sandbox egress policy and enforcement. This control consumes its receipt; egress denial does not inspect the legitimate parser-result channel.
AID-I-001.005 owns safe detonation and raw observation integrity. Parser admission may consume its evidence for hostile-format tests but does not re-score detonation.

controls.name: Software Dependency & Package Security
controls.description_text: At final dependency and package admission in the build or deployment pipeline, verify the complete population of exact resolved package identities, versions, sources, digests, signatures or attestations, SBOM entries, vulnerabilities, yanked status, and license decisions; block when any required artifact or check is missing, stale, unsupported, or fails.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the authoritative build or deployment admission decision for the complete exact population of third-party software packages and build-tool bytes, including identity, source, digest, signature, vulnerability, yanked status, license, and lock resolution.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.001 admits the exact resolved bytes consumed by build or deployment; AID-H-022.002 reviews the proposed dependency change before merge for publisher, repository, name-confusion, and install-behavior risk.
Pre-merge approval is supporting evidence and never pre-authorizes later resolved artifacts.

AID-H-003.001 decides which immutable dependency bytes are approved; AID-H-022.001 installs those approved bytes inside an isolated deterministic environment and exports the consumed dependency layer.
Admission and installation containment are sequential controls with different receipts.

AID-H-003.001 admits third-party packages and build tools before use; AID-H-003.002 gates, signs, and distributes the produced release artifact.
Dependency admission does not establish that the final model release satisfies promotion policy.

AID-H-003.001 evaluates software dependency packages; AID-H-003.009 statically scans model artifacts for malware, unsafe serialization, and loader hazards.
Package security scanning is not a substitute for format-aware model-file analysis.
