AID-H-003.001 admits the exact package and build-tool population before build or deployment; AID-H-003.010 continuously manages vulnerabilities after AI application and platform software is deployed.
A successful admission decision ages and must not be treated as continuing evidence that the deployed fleet remains remediated.

controls.name: CI/CD Release Gating, Model Artifact Signing & Secure Distribution
controls.description_text: Apply mandatory automated acceptance criteria before promoting a model or deployment-bound model package. Verify origin, integrity, provenance, and the exact model-interface files and selectors that ship with the release. Production trusts only immutable, attested bytes from an internal mirror; a signed weight file does not authorize a different tokenizer, chat template, generation configuration, or parser.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns final automated promotion criteria, exact release-package verification, signing, immutable internal mirroring, and secure distribution so production consumes only approved attested model and interface bytes.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.002 gates and signs the completed model release; AID-H-003.001 admits the third-party software and build-tool population used to produce it.
A release can fail promotion despite approved dependencies, and a signed release does not excuse unapproved build inputs.

AID-H-003.002 makes the final promotion and distribution decision; AID-H-003.006 creates the model SBOM and provenance attestation bound to the artifact digest.
The attestation is gate evidence, while the release gate independently verifies and enforces it.

AID-M-002.002 creates and verifies the whole-artifact digest and signature verdict consumed by release policy; AID-H-003.002 owns the final promotion, signing, mirroring, and distribution decision.
A valid integrity verdict is necessary gate evidence but cannot promote a release by itself.

AID-H-003.002 applies the currently approved signature and release policy; AID-H-003.008 makes the active signing and verification path crypto-agile across algorithm and policy migrations.
Promotion semantics and cryptographic migration mechanics remain separate.

AID-H-003.002 gates, signs, and distributes a rebuilt release artifact; AID-H-003.010 determines vulnerability applicability and remediation priority, then verifies rollout completion across the deployed population.
A signed fixed release does not prove that every affected instance received it.

controls.name: External Dataset Supply-Chain Provenance Admission
controls.description_text: Admit an externally supplied dataset only after verifying supplier identity, source provenance, license and use rights, immutable dataset identity, signatures or attestations, lineage, and the complete supplier-policy evidence required by the build or training environment.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns external dataset supplier and provenance admission. It does not characterize the security and privacy properties of the dataset contents or sanitize individual records.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.003 decides whether the dataset's supplier, provenance, rights, signature, and lineage are admissible; AID-M-002.003 characterizes sensitive content, distributions, malformed records, and poisoning indicators.
Trusted provenance does not make content safe, and safe-looking content does not approve an untrusted source.

AID-H-003.003 admits the external source and immutable dataset artifact; AID-H-002.001 sanitizes and quarantines unsafe records in the candidate snapshot.
Supplier admission and record-level content admission must both pass before training use.

controls.name: Hardware/Firmware Attestation & Cluster Admission
controls.description_text: Verify measured boot, accelerator identity, firmware and BIOS/UEFI evidence against a versioned admission policy before a node joins or rejoins an AI cluster. Bind the attestation result to the physical asset, workload identity, approved measurements, verifier version, nonce, and freshness window; stale, missing, replayed, or unverifiable evidence is not an admission pass.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns deployment or cluster admission based on hardware and firmware identity, measured boot or attestation evidence, approved accelerator inventory, freshness, and policy binding. It does not establish purchase custody or manage firmware patching.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.004 consumes trusted boot and hardware identity evidence to admit a node or workload; AID-H-009.001 establishes the hardware root of trust and secure-boot chain.
Root-of-trust evidence is an input, while cluster admission is the policy decision over the exact deployment.

AID-H-003.004 blocks nodes whose firmware or driver state is not approved; AID-H-009.002 owns firmware and driver vulnerability, patch, rollout, and rollback management.
Admission verifies current state but does not perform lifecycle patching.

AID-H-003.004 admits hardware from technical attestation and inventory evidence; AID-H-009.003 verifies purchase receipts, serial custody, shipment authenticity, and tamper-evident handling.
Custody provenance and runtime technical attestation are complementary hardware trust claims.

controls.name: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Security Scanning for AI Systems
controls.description_text: Covers the 'pre-deployment' phase of automatically scanning Infrastructure as Code (IaC) files (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes YAML) in the CI/CD pipeline. This 'shift-left' security practice aims to detect and block security misconfigurations, such as insecure network paths that could undermine model supply chain security, before infrastructure is provisioned.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns security scanning and admission findings for Infrastructure-as-Code that provisions AI compute, storage, network, identity, pipelines, and serving environments before deployment.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.005 scans a concrete IaC change for vulnerabilities and insecure resource definitions; AID-M-005.002 defines the signed policy-as-code baseline, posture criteria, and release gate used to judge configuration.
The scanner evaluates the artifact, while the Model control owns the authoritative configuration-policy contract.

controls.name: Model SBOM & Provenance Attestation
controls.description_text:
Produce a model-centric SBOM that inventories model weights, tokenizer and special-token files, chat template, generation configuration, tool/reasoning parser configuration, model format, and loader code commit; bind every item to the exact release digest through signed in-toto/SLSA provenance.

Interoperability: keep one internal canonical manifest for enforcement, then export standards-compatible AI-BOM formats such as CycloneDX ML-BOM 1.7 and SPDX 3 AI Profile for procurement, regulator, partner exchange, and technical documentation.

Admission control: verify the attestation and digest binding before promotion, and re-verify the same bytes at runtime before loading. This creates a tamper-evident content contract for the complete model interface, not only the weights.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns a signed model SBOM and provenance attestation bound to the exact model release, including weights, tokenizer, special tokens, templates, generation and parser configuration, training inputs, code, frameworks, adapters, build identity, and lineage needed by release admission.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.006 attests the composition and provenance of one exact model release artifact; AID-M-001.002 maintains the broader system dependency map and deployed release composition.
A model SBOM is one artifact-level evidence object, not the complete service and trust-boundary dependency graph.

AID-H-003.006 produces the signed composition and provenance evidence; AID-H-003.002 verifies that evidence and decides whether the release may be promoted and distributed.
Attestation authorship must remain distinguishable from gate enforcement.

AID-H-003.006 describes the complete model release and its components; AID-H-003.007 applies adapter and PEFT-specific identity, base-model binding, provenance, and compatibility admission.
An adapter can have an independent supply chain even when listed in the model SBOM.

controls.name: Adapter / PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning) Supply Chain Integrity & Provenance Verification
controls.description_text: Verify the integrity, provenance, compatibility, and release policy of adapter-based model extensions such as LoRA, QLoRA, and other PEFT artifacts before they are loaded, attached, merged, promoted, or hot-swapped into runtime systems. This sub-technique focuses on preventing trojaned, tampered, incompatible, or untrusted adapters from altering base model behavior through cryptographic verification, publisher/source attestation, strict binding to the intended base model and runtime, registry allowlisting, and post-load behavioral validation.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns supply-chain integrity and provenance verification for adapters, LoRA and PEFT artifacts, including immutable identity, source, signature, base-model binding, configuration, compatibility, and loader constraints before composition.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.007 admits an adapter and proves its exact base-model and configuration binding; AID-H-003.006 attests the composition and provenance of the complete model release.
Adapter-specific admission precedes and feeds the release SBOM rather than disappearing into it.

AID-H-003.007 verifies adapter source, identity, signature, and compatibility; AID-H-003.009 scans model and adapter files for unsafe serialization and malware.
Provenance does not prove safe loader behavior, and a clean static scan does not establish trusted origin.

controls.name: Crypto-Agile Artifact Signing & Distribution (PQC-Ready)
controls.description_text: Design AI artifact signing and distribution workflows so they can change cryptographic algorithms, verifier policy, and signature requirements over time without breaking release governance. The active build-to-distribution path for models, checkpoints, adapters, containers, manifests, and attestations should support algorithm agility, staged dual-sign or hybrid-sign migration, and verifier-policy updates before promotion or consumption.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns cryptographic agility in the active build-to-distribution path, including algorithm migration, dual-sign periods, verifier-policy evolution, and preservation of required signature sets across redistribution. It does not define release acceptance semantics or archive-lifetime trust continuity.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.008 governs how signing algorithms and verifier requirements evolve; AID-H-003.002 defines and enforces the artifact promotion gate under the active approved policy.
Changing cryptography must not silently change release acceptance criteria.

AID-H-003.008 protects active build and distribution during cryptographic migration; AID-M-002.005 preserves classical-plus-post-quantum trust continuity across years of archival storage, rollover, and restore.
Operational distribution agility and long-lived archive provenance have different timelines and verification chains.

AID-H-003.008 governs the signature infrastructure and verifier policy; AID-H-003.006 governs the model SBOM and provenance content bound to the artifact.
Crypto agility changes how evidence is signed, not what composition facts the attestation must contain.

controls.name: Model Artifact Static Malware & Unsafe-Serialization Scanning
controls.description_text: Statically scan model artifacts, checkpoints, adapters, and packaged model bundles before they are imported, mirrored, loaded, promoted, or deployed. The control inspects serialized model bytes and archive members for unsafe deserialization primitives, dangerous pickle globals, embedded code, custom loader requirements, unexpected scripts, and model-format policy violations without executing the artifact.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns format-aware static malware, unsafe-serialization, archive, and loader-hazard scanning of model artifacts before any model loader executes them. Its clean verdict is admission evidence, not proof of safe execution.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.009 scans model artifact formats and serialized objects; AID-H-003.001 evaluates third-party software dependencies and packages.
Model-file loader hazards require dedicated format semantics beyond package SCA.

AID-H-003.009 determines whether the artifact contains known unsafe serialization or malware indicators; AID-H-003.006 verifies the artifact's declared composition and provenance.
A trusted attestation does not make unsafe bytes executable, and a clean scan does not establish provenance.

AID-H-003.009 performs static analysis before any loader runs; AID-I-001.005 detonates and observes first load inside an isolated sandbox.
Dynamic loading can reveal behavior that static scanners miss, while sandbox execution must not replace pre-load rejection.

AID-H-003.009 analyzes serialized model and adapter artifacts; AID-H-025.001 analyzes generated code and execution requests for dangerous constructs.
Both are pre-execution gates, but they operate on different artifact languages and loaders.

AID-H-003.009 statically scans models, checkpoints, and adapters for unsafe serialization and embedded code; AID-H-002.009 admits untrusted dataset and structured-data artifacts against parser-specific features.
Route each object by its actual format and loader; a model-artifact scan does not make a dataset parser safe, and parser admission does not approve model loading.

controls.name: Deployed AI Software Vulnerability Remediation Lifecycle
controls.description_text: Continuously identify and remediate known vulnerabilities in deployed AI software components, including inference servers, orchestration frameworks, agent and MCP runtimes or SDKs, plugins, containers, and supporting libraries after initial admission. Maintain a versioned deployed-component inventory, ecosystem-specific advisory coverage, policy-defined remediation deadlines, rebuild-and-redeploy updates, staged rollout and rollback, and time-bound compensating controls when a compatible fix is unavailable. Close a finding only after independent fleet readback proves the affected population is remediated or an approved exception remains effective.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns continuous vulnerability discovery, prioritization, remediation decisions, compatible rebuild or replacement, staged deployment, rollback, compensating-control expiry, and complete-fleet verification for deployed AI software after initial build or deployment admission.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.010 continuously remediates vulnerabilities disclosed in deployed software; AID-H-003.001 decides whether exact dependency bytes may enter a build or deployment.
Admission is a point-in-time gate, while remediation maintains the approved posture throughout operation.

AID-H-003.010 owns the need, deadline, staged rollout, rollback, and fleet closure for a software remediation; AID-H-003.002 owns final promotion, signing, and distribution of an approved release artifact.
A remediation normally uses the release gate, but passing that gate does not prove the vulnerable deployed population was replaced.

AID-H-003.010 covers AI application, framework, runtime, SDK, plugin, container, and library software; AID-H-009.002 covers accelerator firmware and drivers.
The inventories, compatibility constraints, rollout mechanisms, and recovery evidence differ even when one change requires coordinated testing with the other.

AID-H-003.010 decides whether deployed software must be upgraded, rebuilt, replaced, disabled, or temporarily isolated and verifies fleet completion; AID-H-028.006 verifies MCP client, plugin, and update authenticity and integrity.
Update authenticity answers whether bytes are trusted, not whether remediation is timely, compatible, complete, or still required.

controls.name: Attested Edge Model Entitlement & Key Release
controls.description_text: When protected model weights are distributed to a client or edge device outside the enterprise trust boundary, keep the package encrypted and release its content key only after the server verifies a fresh, request-bound app/device attestation and the authenticated subject's entitlement to the exact model release. Bind the decision to the app identity, device or workload key, release digest, challenge, policy, and expiry; deny release when verification is unavailable or incomplete.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns entitlement and fresh platform-attestation enforcement at the protected client/edge model key-release point, including request binding, replay prevention, exact release identity, wrapped-key delivery, and release evidence. It does not sign model packages, establish the user identity, or claim that attestation prevents all post-release extraction.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-003.002 signs, promotes, and distributes the exact model release package; AID-H-003.011 decides whether one client or edge subject may receive its decryption key.
Artifact authenticity does not establish recipient entitlement, and an entitled recipient must still receive only an approved signed release.

AID-H-004.001 establishes and authorizes the human or privileged subject; AID-H-003.011 consumes that authenticated identity together with device/app attestation at the model-key release point.
Neither a valid login nor a valid device verdict alone is sufficient to release protected model bytes.

AID-H-003.011 controls decryption-key release for a model intentionally distributed to a client or edge device; AID-H-009.005 protects inference inside an attested confidential-computing boundary.
Client-side distribution accepts bounded residual extraction risk after release, while confidential inference keeps the model inside a protected execution environment.

AID-H-003.011 decides whether an entitled, freshly attested client may receive the content key for an exact model release; AID-I-007 confines what the client-side model runtime can access after execution begins.
Key-release admission does not prove client-runtime isolation, and isolation does not authorize delivery of protected model bytes.

AID-H-003.011 controls entitlement and decryption-key release before protected model bytes become usable on a client; AID-H-013 embeds or evaluates bounded provenance and ownership signals after an artifact or its outputs may be copied.
A watermark or fingerprint is not an entitlement decision, and attested delivery does not provide later ownership attribution.

controls.name: User & Privileged Access Management
controls.description_text: Focuses on securing access for human users, such as developers, data scientists, and system administrators, who manage and interact with AI systems. The goal is to enforce strong authentication and granular permissions for human identities.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns authentication, least privilege, privileged-access management, recertification, and deprovisioning for human developers, operators, data scientists, reviewers, and administrators accessing AI systems.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-004.001 governs human and privileged identities; AID-H-004.002 authenticates workloads, services, jobs, applications, and external machine integrations.
Human MFA and PAM do not establish workload identity, while service credentials do not grant a person privileged access.

controls.name: Service & API Authentication
controls.description_text: Authenticate every workload, service, application, job, and external integration before an AI API, data store, or MLOps handler receives its request. At the gateway, service mesh, or service boundary, verify issuer, audience, workload identity, credential freshness, proof, and route binding, and reject delivery on any mismatch.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns machine identity authentication at API, service-mesh, gateway, data-store, and MLOps boundaries, including issuer, audience, workload identity, credential freshness, proof, and route binding. It proves identity but does not by itself grant business-data authorization.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-004.002 authenticates non-human workloads and services; AID-H-004.001 governs human and privileged users.
The credential types, lifecycle, assurance methods, and review populations are different.

AID-H-004.002 establishes the calling machine or workload identity; AID-H-004.003 protects the complete live agent-to-agent message and task protocol, including replay, sequence, context ownership, and per-request authorization.
Authenticated transport identity is necessary but insufficient for secure agent interaction semantics.

AID-H-004.002 authenticates a machine or workload at the channel or service boundary; AID-H-004.005 preserves applicable security-relevant message content, context, freshness, and replay state across the complete path.
Authentication at one hop does not establish end-to-end message integrity after termination, forwarding, queuing, or asynchronous delivery.

controls.name: Secure Agent-to-Agent Communication
controls.description_text: Secure the live request path between agents in custom, MCP-adjacent, and standards-based Agent2Agent (A2A) deployments. Each receiver verifies the authenticated peer, protocol version, payload integrity, replay state, task/context ownership, valid task transition, stream order, push-callback authenticity, and per-request authorization before exposing task data or accepting work.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns receiver-side security for live agent-to-agent requests and streams, including peer authentication, protocol and payload integrity, replay state, task and context ownership, state transitions, stream order, callback authenticity, and per-request authorization.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-004.003 enforces the A2A message and task lifecycle after peer identity is established; AID-H-004.002 authenticates the underlying workload, service, or API caller.
Machine authentication does not validate message replay, task state, protocol binding, or delegation context.

AID-H-004.003 secures the selected live peer communication path; AID-H-004.004 verifies discovery records, Agent Cards, endpoint selection, and advertised capability provenance before that path is chosen.
Discovery trust precedes communication enforcement but does not replace it.

AID-H-004.003 validates each receiver-side message and task transition; AID-H-017.006 constrains the end-to-end delegation graph, hop and loop bounds, and capability attenuation across multiple agents.
Per-hop transport security and whole-chain delegation safety are separate controls.

AID-H-004.003 rejects replayed or misbound agent messages; AID-H-018.008 prevents duplicate external side effects from retries, redelivery, resume, and uncertain outcomes.
Message replay resistance does not guarantee that a provider effect executes at most once.

AID-H-004.003 owns A2A peer, task and context ownership, state-transition, stream-order, callback, and per-request authorization semantics; AID-H-004.005 owns the generic end-to-end message envelope and replay primitive across applicable trust boundaries.
The A2A control remains independently implementable and must not be reduced to a reference to the generic primitive.

controls.name: Verified Agent Discovery, Agent Cards & Registry Provenance
controls.description_text:
Verify agent discovery metadata before an agent endpoint, capability manifest, or registry record is trusted.

A2A deployments: verify signed Agent Cards and bind the verified endpoint, protocol version, and capability manifest to the routing decision.

ANS-style deployments: require signed name-resolution records, RA/CA lifecycle controls, TTL-based revalidation, and mandatory revocation checks (CRL/OCSP). ANS is a registry/name-service design pattern; A2A Agent Cards are the cross-vendor protocol artifact when A2A is the deployed interoperability layer. This defense prevents registry poisoning, identity impersonation, capability forgery, and stale endpoint reuse.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns verification of Agent Cards, discovery records, registry and name-resolution provenance, endpoint and protocol selection, advertised capabilities, TTL, and revocation before an agent route is trusted.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-004.004 proves which endpoint and advertised capability record may be used; AID-H-004.003 secures the actual message, stream, task, and authorization lifecycle after connection.
A verified Agent Card does not authorize every later request.

AID-H-004.004 verifies agent-level discovery and endpoint provenance; AID-H-024 resolves and pins tool or MCP names, versions, descriptors, and contracts.
Agent identity discovery and tool-resolution integrity operate at different namespaces.

controls.name: End-to-End Message Integrity, Freshness & Replay Protection
controls.description_text:
Protect security-relevant AI messages end to end when transport security cannot preserve one authenticated channel from the original sender to the final consumer.

Applicability: Use a deterministic signed envelope and atomic replay rejection for paths with terminating gateways or proxies, multi-hop TLS, queues or event buses, store-and-forward delivery, asynchronous webhooks or callbacks, cross-tenant or administrative boundaries, security-critical commands, or TLS 0-RTT and retry exposure. Bind the sender, audience, operation, target, exact content bytes, validity window, unique message ID, and, when required, the originating request.

Not applicable: Only when complete signed path inventory and independent topology readback prove that none of these conditions exists; mTLS alone is not sufficient evidence.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the conditional, protocol-independent end-to-end envelope profile for exact message-byte integrity, sender and audience binding, operation and target binding, policy-defined freshness, atomic single-use replay state, key rotation, and conditional request-response binding across AI communication paths whose transport is insufficient.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-004.005 authenticates and freshness-binds a message across intermediaries; AID-H-004.002 authenticates the workload, service, API caller, and protected channel.
Transport or caller authentication is necessary but may end at a proxy, queue, or session boundary before the message reaches its final consumer.

AID-H-004.005 provides the generic end-to-end envelope integrity and replay primitive; AID-H-004.003 owns A2A peer, task/context ownership, state transition, stream order, callback, and per-request authorization semantics.
A2A deployments retain their protocol-native checks and add this primitive only on applicable message paths.

AID-H-004.005 atomically rejects an altered, stale, or reused message envelope; AID-H-018.008 prevents duplicate external side effects across retries, redelivery, and ambiguous outcomes.
Single-use message acceptance does not guarantee exactly-once provider behavior, and an idempotency key does not prove message authenticity.

AID-H-004.005 provides the reusable end-to-end message-envelope primitive across untrusted intermediaries; AID-H-012.004 owns authenticity, freshness, producer identity, and consumption binding for externally computed reward payloads.
When the message is a learning reward, the reward-channel result is scored only under AID-H-012.004 rather than again as a generic envelope PASS.

AID-H-004.005 owns a generic envelope profile across untrusted or asynchronous intermediaries; AID-H-034 owns MCP-specific transport, OAuth, routing, handles, Tasks, subscriptions, operation budgets, idempotency boundaries, and disable-state enforcement.
MCP-specific nonce, proof-of-possession, handle, task, or commit-fence mechanisms remain with their MCP controls and do not replace an applicable end-to-end envelope.

controls.name: Hosted Agent Publication & Exposure Controls
controls.description_text:
Prevent unintended access to agents published through vendor-hosted and low-code platforms. The tenant platform administrator and agent release owner enforce approved audiences, channels, sharing boundaries, and connector execution identities before publication and after configuration changes.

Applies to organizations publishing agents on shared provider infrastructure, including provider-owned hostnames; merely consuming a vendor assistant is outside this control. Shipping tenant data policies, channel restrictions, and agent administration interfaces provide the implementation path. Public agents are allowed only through a versioned exception whose reachable knowledge, tools, and identities are appropriate for anonymous users.

Evidence combines effective tenant and agent configuration, complete published-agent inventory, denied publication attempts, and independent access probes against the published version. No applicable hosted agents means NOT_APPLICABLE; incomplete inventory or unavailable effective permissions means INSUFFICIENT_DATA, collection failure means ERROR, and reachable unauthorized capabilities mean FAIL. PASS requires both preventive settings and successful negative access tests for the applicable population. This publication gate also covers the release of provider-native event-trigger configurations. Where the hosted platform has no tenant-controlled pre-run admission point, verify the native trigger filters, approved event resources and dedicated execution identity here; a configured maker connection does not prove per-event initiator authorization. Missing supplier evidence remains INSUFFICIENT_DATA, and an unenforceable required restriction prevents release.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the technical release and configuration-drift gate for hosted agents: who can reach each published agent and which channels, shared connections, and knowledge sources that audience can exercise.

related_techniques.comparison: Discovery supplies the hosted-tenant population and exposure findings; this control configures and verifies the publication restrictions.
Reuse workload authentication; a service identity alone does not establish the audience of a published SaaS agent.
Event-to-run authority is checked at trigger admission; publication approval does not authorize each external event.
Runtime per-action authorization remains independent of the publication gate.
Containment owns disabling access after a finding; this control owns release denial and exposure configuration.

controls.name: External Event-to-Agent Admission & Authority Binding
controls.description_text:
Authorize externally delivered email, webhook, or messaging events before they create an agent run. The integration receiver and workflow owner distinguish authenticated delivery from the initiating actor's authority, select an approved workflow and execution identity from trusted configuration, and preserve that binding through queues and workers.

This applies when externally controlled events can initiate agent activity; an agent with no such triggers is NOT_APPLICABLE. Shipping event-driven agent platforms and demonstrated probing of agent trigger channels anchor this control. Provider signatures or aligned email domains alone do not authorize use of the agent maker's privileges.

Verify rejected-source, wrong-workspace, unauthorized-actor, replay, and altered-routing events against the actual receiver and worker. PASS requires correct run admission and unchanged authority across the applicable trigger population; an unauthorized run is FAIL, missing provider/actor evidence is INSUFFICIENT_DATA, and verification or policy-service failure is ERROR with admission denied. Applies to tenant-controlled event receivers/workflows, or platform-supported pre-run admission adapters that expose verifiable initiator/resource binding. A provider-native trigger with no such tenant integration point is NOT_APPLICABLE to this receiver control; AID-H-004.006 owns its hosted publication and native-trigger restrictions. If the admission architecture exists but its evidence or required adapter is missing, report INSUFFICIENT_DATA or ERROR rather than NOT_APPLICABLE.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the external-event-to-agent-run boundary: authorized initiator, event resource, workflow, execution identity, and bounded task authority before scheduling.

related_techniques.comparison: Reuse provider-native integrity, freshness, and durable replay protection; a valid delivery signature is not initiator authorization.
Consume registered workload identities and delegation context; registration does not authorize an external event to start a run.
The admitted task bounds downstream capabilities; runtime scoping can only narrow the admitted authority.
Per-tool/service action authorization remains a later gate and does not substitute for event admission.
Effect idempotency is separate from deduplicating event delivery and run creation.

Hosted publication owns native trigger configuration when the provider exposes no tenant-controlled pre-run admission point. This receiver gate does not independently score the same hosted configuration or treat maker credentials as initiator authority.

controls.name: Differential Privacy for AI
controls.description_text: Implements differential privacy mechanisms to add calibrated noise to model training, outputs, or data queries, ensuring that individual data points cannot be identified while maintaining overall utility.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns quantified differential-privacy mechanisms, clipping and noise calibration, privacy-budget composition, and utility validation for training, outputs, queries, or local collection.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-005.001 provides a quantified differential-privacy guarantee under an explicit accountant and threat model; AID-H-005.003 provides empirical non-DP memorization and confidence-leakage reduction through regularization.
Empirical attack improvement must not be described as a formal DP guarantee.

controls.name: Homomorphic Encryption for AI
controls.description_text: Apply homomorphic encryption so supported AI computations operate on ciphertext and plaintext is not exposed to the untrusted compute path. Pure HE workflows keep protected values encrypted throughout the evaluated computation; hybrid HE-plus-TEE workflows may decrypt only inside measured enclave memory for operations that the HE circuit cannot support, then re-encrypt before data leaves the attested boundary. Applicability depends on a model and operator set that can be represented within the selected scheme, precision, multiplicative-depth, key-management, and latency constraints.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns privacy-preserving supported computation over ciphertext, including scheme, precision, multiplicative depth, key management, operator coverage, and explicit hybrid HE-plus-attested-enclave transitions.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-005.002 protects data by evaluating supported operations over ciphertext and may use an enclave only for unsupported operations; AID-H-009.005 protects plaintext computation inside a remotely attested confidential runtime.
Homomorphic encryption and trusted-execution confidentiality have different plaintext exposure, operator, and trust assumptions.

controls.name: Training-Time Privacy Regularization
controls.description_text: Reduce record-level memorization and confidence leakage by applying one governed, non-differentially-private regularization mechanism during training and requiring the defended candidate to improve the policy-selected membership-inference evaluation without exceeding the signed utility budget for the model family. The signed profile selects mixup, calibrated input noise, or label smoothing and binds that mechanism to the candidate and evaluation population.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns one governed non-differentially-private training regularization profile and empirical evidence that it reduces policy-selected membership-inference risk within the utility budget. It makes no formal privacy guarantee.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-005.003 provides empirical privacy hardening through mixup, input noise, or label smoothing; AID-H-005.001 provides a quantified differential-privacy guarantee.
Use the DP control when a formal epsilon and delta claim is required.

AID-H-005.003 changes model training to reduce memorization risk; AID-H-005.004 removes duplicate and near-duplicate corpus content before training.
Data-centric deduplication and model-training regularization address different causes of memorization.

controls.name: LLM Training Data Deduplication
controls.description_text: A data-centric hardening technique that involves systematically removing duplicate or near-duplicate sequences from the training datasets for Large Language Models (LLMs). This pre-processing step directly mitigates the risk of unintended memorization, where LLMs are prone to learn and regenerate specific training examples verbatim, which can lead to the leakage of sensitive or copyrighted information.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns exact and near-duplicate removal from LLM training corpora before training, together with coverage evidence and post-training memorization checks for the deduplication objective.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-005.004 reduces repeated exposure by changing the training corpus; AID-H-005.003 changes the training objective or inputs through a non-DP regularization mechanism.
Deduplication does not provide regularization, and regularization does not remove duplicated sensitive passages.

controls.name: Embedding & Vector Store Confidentiality
controls.description_text: Treat embeddings and vector-store contents as sensitive derived data, not harmless indexes. This sub-technique protects raw embedding vectors, vector-store exports, snapshots, backups, logs, and debugging dumps from disclosure or misuse that could enable embedding inversion, membership inference, or reconstruction of source records. It covers PII minimization before embedding, encryption of vector storage and backups, strict prohibition of raw vector export except through approved break-glass paths, and documented privacy-utility tradeoffs for noise, perturbation, or differential-privacy controls.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns confidentiality and inversion-resistance controls for raw embeddings, vector-store exports, snapshots, backups, logs, and debug surfaces, including minimization before embedding, encryption, and raw-vector export restrictions.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-005.005 protects embedding and vector data from disclosure or reconstruction; AID-H-020.003 authorizes which documents and chunks a requester may retrieve.
Storage confidentiality and query-time document authorization are independent protections.

AID-H-005.005 protects vector artifacts and exports as sensitive derived data; AID-H-032.002 isolates cross-tenant serving state such as KV caches, batches, allocators, and reusable buffers.
Vector-store confidentiality does not isolate inference-engine state.

AID-H-005.005 owns embedding-specific confidentiality and export controls; AID-I-004.002 owns persistent tenant and trust partitioning for memory and knowledge namespaces.
A partition boundary controls who can address records, while confidentiality controls how vector data is stored and exposed.

controls.name: Structured Output Enforcement
controls.description_text: Require model output and any extracted tool-call or reasoning fields to conform to a strict predefined schema and bounded parser contract before downstream use. Reject ambiguous, duplicated, malformed, truncated, or out-of-contract structures instead of repairing them into an action.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns deterministic conformance of model output to a predefined structured schema and verifies the bounded parser that extracts tool calls, reasoning fields, and visible content from raw generation before downstream use.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-006.001 proves structural schema conformance; AID-H-006.002 applies sink-specific encoding, URL policy, redaction, remote-subresource removal, streaming holdback, and final text or markup release.
Schema-valid content can still be unsafe for its destination.

controls.name: Text, Markup & Structured Output Sanitization and Release Gate
controls.description_text: Enforce the preventive boundary between generated text, markup, structured payloads, URLs, and a user or downstream system. Apply sink-specific encoding, schema and URL validation, sensitive-data redaction, remote-subresource removal, and a streaming holdback gate.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns sanitization and final release of generated text, markup, structured payloads, URLs, and token streams to a specific sink. It does not own non-text media or binary release and does not authorize code execution.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-006.002 protects the actual destination through encoding, redaction, URL controls, and holdback; AID-H-006.001 enforces only the structured schema.
Structure is one input to sink safety rather than the complete release decision.

AID-H-006.002 releases text, markup, URLs, and token streams; AID-H-006.004 safely decodes, re-encodes, scans, quarantines, or releases generated media and binary artifacts.
Use the content-derived artifact type rather than the model's declared MIME type to choose the boundary.

AID-H-006.002 prevents generated text or code from creating unsafe sink behavior during release; AID-H-025 decides whether generated code or an execution request may run and under which interpreter.
A safely displayed script is not approved executable code.

AID-H-006.002 owns sink-specific release of model-generated text, markup, URLs, structured payloads, and token streams; AID-H-002.009 owns dataset-parser admission and its conditional bounded-row preview method.
For a mixed response, apply each control to its own segment and assign one primary release-gate result to the final bytes rather than double-scoring the same publication.

AID-H-006.002 owns sink-specific release of generated text, markup, structured payloads, URLs, and token streams; AID-H-018.009 confines the local filesystem object that an applicable model-callable handler actually opens or mutates.
A path-broker receipt can be an input to release, but it neither sanitizes returned content nor earns a second sink-safety PASS.

controls.name: Prediction Response Minimization & Extraction-Resistance Validation
controls.description_text:
Expose only the numeric prediction detail required by an explicit API contract through one versioned response profile. For a minimization transform, gate release on a model-family query suite showing reduced extraction signal within utility and API-contract budgets. If calibrated probabilities are required, explicitly bind the permitted fields and precision to that contract, retain calibration and extraction-risk review, and enforce compensating access and query-abuse controls. Keeping required precision is not evidence that extraction risk was reduced.

Applicability: use only for APIs that expose classifier confidence or continuous predictions. If the API already returns no numeric model signal, this control does not apply. A configured bin, rounding rule, or noise flag alone is insufficient. This control makes no differential-privacy claim and rejects raw logits and probability fields outside the approved response contract.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns contract-bounded response detail for numeric prediction APIs, including explicit calibrated-probability release decisions, and independent validation that rounding, binning, range reduction, or approved noise lowers extraction signal within utility and API-contract budgets. It makes no differential-privacy claim.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-006.003 empirically reduces externally exposed prediction precision; AID-H-005.001 provides a quantified differential-privacy guarantee through calibrated noise and accounting.
Response minimization must not be represented as DP unless the full privacy mechanism and accountant apply.

controls.name: Generated Media & Binary Artifact Output Safety Release Gate
controls.description_text: Treat every model-generated image, audio, video, PDF, office document, archive, or other binary artifact as untrusted bytes. Strictly decode the representation, enforce byte and decompression bounds, identify the actual type from content, reject executable or polyglot content, and either canonicalize through an approved decoder and encoder or quarantine for malware scanning and content disarm. Release only transformed bytes after checking their type, digest, policy binding, and required security results against the exact output bytes.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns preventive decode, type validation, bounds, canonical re-encoding, malware or content-disarm evidence, quarantine, and final release for generated media and binary artifacts.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-006.004 owns non-text media and binary artifact release; AID-H-006.002 owns text, markup, URL, structured-payload, and token-stream release.
A document may require bounded text extraction, but its container and embedded objects still belong to the binary gate.

AID-H-006.004 transforms, quarantines, blocks, or releases the generated artifact; AID-D-003.008 emits policy, malware, type, and coverage findings over it.
The detector supplies evidence, while this control owns the release decision.

AID-H-006.004 rejects executable or unsafe binary output from release; AID-H-025 governs whether code or commands may be executed in a controlled runtime.
Artifact release and execution admission remain separate even when the same bytes are involved.

controls.name: Secure Training Environment Provisioning
controls.description_text: This sub-technique focuses on the infrastructure layer of AI security. It covers the creation of dedicated, isolated, and hardened environments for training jobs using Infrastructure as Code (IaC), least-privilege IAM roles, and, where necessary, confidential computing. The goal is to build a secure foundation for the training process, protecting it from both internal and external threats, and ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of the data and model being processed.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns creation of dedicated, isolated, least-privilege, and hardened training environments, including network, identity, compute, storage, IaC, and confidential-computing boundaries before a job starts.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-007.001 provisions the trusted environment and permissions for a training job; AID-H-007.002 monitors the running job's behavior, stability, metrics, and audit trail.
A hardened environment does not prove the job behaved correctly after launch.

controls.name: Runtime Training Job Monitoring & Auditing
controls.description_text: Focuses on instrumenting the training script itself to continuously monitor for behavioral anomalies and to create a detailed, immutable audit log. This involves real-time tracking of key training metrics (e.g., loss, gradient norms) to detect signs of instability or poisoning, and systematically logging all parameters, code versions, and data versions to ensure any training run is fully auditable and reproducible.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns runtime training-job instrumentation, anomaly and stability checks, controlled termination, and immutable audit records for metrics, code, data, parameters, environment, and produced artifacts.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-007.002 observes and controls the running training job; AID-H-007.001 establishes the isolated infrastructure and least-privilege execution environment.
Runtime evidence and environment provisioning are separately verifiable controls.

AID-H-007.002 records and responds to behavior during the original run; AID-H-007.003 captures the complete run manifest and independently replays it for reproducibility.
A detailed audit trail is necessary but does not establish that another environment can reproduce the result.

controls.name: Training Process Reproducibility
controls.description_text: For every training run, create an immutable manifest binding source commit, configuration, dependency lock, dataset/version digest, seed, builder and runtime image digest, hardware/runtime settings, and produced model digest. Before promotion, independently replay the exact manifest in an approved environment and compare declared outputs and policy-bounded tolerances; missing inputs, non-replayable state, or unexplained divergence fails the gate.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns immutable training-run capture and independent replay of source, configuration, dependency lock, dataset, seed, images, hardware settings, runtime, and produced model, including policy-bounded divergence decisions. It does not prove each input is trustworthy or the model is safe.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-007.003 proves whether the exact run can be replayed from its bound inputs; AID-H-007.002 monitors and audits the original running job.
Reproducibility and runtime anomaly detection answer different integrity questions.

AID-H-007.003 proves run reconstruction and output consistency; AID-H-007.004 proves that evaluation data, suites, independence, sufficiency, and promotion evidence are trustworthy.
A reproducible model can still be evaluated on manipulated or inadequate evidence.

controls.name: Evaluation Data Integrity, Sufficiency Assurance & Promotion Governance
controls.description_text:
Ensure the integrity, independence, and sufficiency of evaluation artifacts used in validation and promotion decisions. This includes evaluation datasets, holdout sets, benchmarks, safety test suites, and security regression corpora.

What this covers: Existing techniques already address training environment security, reproducibility, detector-specific evaluation, and benchmark execution, but this sub-technique provides a general-purpose evaluation security discipline that applies across model types and promotion workflows.

Threat model: The threat model is simple but high impact: if an attacker can manipulate evaluation data or evaluation evidence, a compromised model can appear to pass all validation gates and be promoted as if it were safe.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns integrity, independence, sufficiency, freshness, leakage checks, and release binding for evaluation datasets, holdouts, benchmarks, safety suites, regression corpora, raw results, and promotion evidence. It does not execute every specialized benchmark or own evaluator implementation.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-007.004 secures evaluation populations and promotion evidence; AID-H-007.003 secures capture and reproducibility of the training run.
Replaying training does not establish evaluation independence or sufficiency.

AID-H-007.004 governs general evaluation evidence and promotion use; AID-H-007.005 owns the specific pre/post safety-alignment regression gate for fine-tuned or customized models.
The specialized gate consumes general evidence-integrity controls but has a distinct measured candidate and outcome.

AID-H-007.004 protects cases, datasets, corpus coverage, and result binding; AID-H-007.007 protects the judge model, grader code, rubric, harness, thresholds, and evidence writer that interpret captured behavior.
Trusted cases can still be mis-scored by a compromised evaluator.

AID-H-007.004 secures benchmark data, independence, sufficiency, and evidence; AID-M-008 executes adversarial agent security benchmark campaigns.
Benchmark execution does not own the integrity of its holdout and promotion evidence.

AID-H-007.004 protects evaluation independence, corpus sufficiency, holdout isolation, and promotion evidence; AID-H-002.001 sanitizes the content of candidate evaluation records before an evaluation job can read them.
An independent, sufficient, and leak-free evaluation corpus can still contain poisoned or privacy-sensitive records.

controls.name: Fine-Tuning Safety Alignment Preservation & Erosion Detection
controls.description_text: Gate fine-tuned, adapter-tuned, instruction-tuned, RLHF/RLAIF-updated, or otherwise customized models against a pre/post safety regression suite before promotion. The control compares the tuned model to an approved baseline on refusal behavior, harmful-content compliance, jailbreak and prompt-injection resistance, tool-use policy adherence, and sensitive-data leakage. Promotion is blocked when the tuned model materially erodes safety alignment even if ordinary task-quality metrics improve.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the pre/post safety-alignment regression gate for fine-tuned, adapter-tuned, instruction-tuned, RLHF or RLAIF-updated, and otherwise customized target models, blocking promotion on policy-defined safety erosion.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-007.005 evaluates safety erosion caused by model customization; AID-H-007.004 governs integrity and sufficiency of the evaluation population and promotion evidence.
The safety delta gate consumes but does not replace evaluation governance.

AID-H-007.005 covers changes that customize model behavior through fine-tuning or alignment training; AID-H-007.006 covers deployment artifacts and serving pairings derived from an already approved source through quantization, pruning, conversion, merge, distillation, or compilation.
Choose ownership from the transformation that produced the candidate, not merely from the output format.

AID-H-007.005 evaluates the safety alignment of the tuned model being promoted; AID-H-036 evaluates the multilingual and locale-stratified performance of prompt-safety classifiers.
The protected model and the guardrail classifier are different evaluation subjects.

controls.name: Post-Training Optimization & Format-Conversion Safety Regression
controls.description_text: Treat every derived deployment artifact or serving-time model/interface pairing as a security-relevant change. Require signed source-to-candidate lineage and a pre/post behavioral regression gate. This includes quantization, pruning, distillation, weight or adapter merges, ONNX/GGUF/TensorRT conversion, speculative-decoding pairs, and changes to the tokenizer, special tokens, chat template, generation configuration, or tool/reasoning parser. Fail promotion when lineage or required evaluation coverage is missing, or when task quality, jailbreak, prompt injection, leakage, harmful content, structured output, reasoning extraction, or tool policy regresses beyond policy.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns source-to-candidate lineage and pre/post behavioral regression for quantization, pruning, distillation, merges, format conversion, runtime engine compilation, and serving-time model/interface pairings derived from an approved source.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-007.006 evaluates safety change from post-training optimization, conversion, or derived serving artifacts; AID-H-007.005 evaluates safety erosion from fine-tuning and behavioral customization.
Distillation belongs here when it creates a deployment-derived student from an approved source, even though its derivation uses training.

AID-H-007.006 verifies transformation-specific lineage and behavioral delta; AID-H-003.006 owns the general model SBOM and provenance attestation.
The transformation gate adds source-to-candidate evidence without becoming the canonical composition record.

controls.name: Evaluator, Judge & Test-Harness Integrity
controls.description_text: Protect the evaluator mechanism that turns captured candidate behavior into scores and gate decisions: judge-model digests, grader or scoring code, rubric and judge-prompt templates, dependencies, harness orchestration, threshold policy, and evidence-writer configuration. Prevent the evaluated system or its identity from reading protected evaluator internals or modifying evaluator inputs, logic, results, or signatures.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns integrity and independence of the evaluator mechanism: judge model, grader and scoring code, rubric, judge prompts, dependencies, harness orchestration, threshold policy, and evidence-writer configuration. It does not own test-case sufficiency or adversarial coverage.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-007.007 protects how captured behavior is scored and converted into a gate decision; AID-H-007.004 protects the evaluation cases, holdouts, corpus sufficiency, leakage boundaries, and result binding.
Evaluator integrity and evaluation-data integrity must be verified independently.

AID-H-007.007 protects the judge and harness mechanism; AID-M-008 owns the adversarial benchmark scenarios and their execution against the agent.
A secure evaluator does not establish adequate attack coverage.

controls.name: Secure Aggregation Protocols for Federated Learning
controls.description_text: Employs cryptographic methods in Federated Learning (FL) to protect the privacy of individual client contributions, such as model updates or gradients.  These protocols are designed so the central server can compute the aggregate (sum or average) of all client updates but cannot inspect or reverse-engineer any individual contribution.  This hardens the FL process against inference attacks by the server and preserves user privacy in collaborative learning environments.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns cryptographic confidentiality of individual federated client contributions while enabling policy-approved aggregate computation and dropout recovery.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-008.001 hides individual client updates from the aggregator; AID-H-008.002 requires individual updates or equivalent verifiable statistics to filter Byzantine influence.
Ordinary secure-sum and conventional per-client robust aggregation cannot both be claimed without a specifically reviewed compatible protocol or confidential boundary.

AID-H-008.001 protects the confidentiality of contributions from participants already accepted into a round; AID-H-008.003 authenticates and admits the participant and exact round-bound update.
Contribution privacy does not establish that a submitter is authorized or benign.

controls.name: Byzantine-Robust Aggregation Rules
controls.description_text: A class of statistical, non-cryptographic aggregation methods designed to protect the integrity of the global model in Federated Learning. These rules identify and mitigate the impact of outlier or malicious model updates from compromised clients (Byzantine actors) by using functions like median, trimmed mean, or distance-based scoring (e.g., Krum) to filter out or down-weight anomalous contributions before they can corrupt the final aggregated model.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns statistical filtering, down-weighting, or exclusion of anomalous and Byzantine federated updates before they corrupt the global model. It does not provide individual-contribution confidentiality.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-008.002 controls malicious-update influence using per-client statistics or equivalent proofs; AID-H-008.001 hides each client's update under secure aggregation.
Deploy both only through an explicitly compatible privacy-preserving robust protocol or trusted aggregation boundary.

AID-H-008.002 limits the influence of accepted updates even from authorized but malicious clients; AID-H-008.003 decides whether the identity and exact update may enter the round.
Authorized participation is not proof of benign contribution.

controls.name: Federated Participant Enrollment, Attestation & Round Admission
controls.description_text: Admit a federated-learning participant only when its organization-approved identity, current workload attestation, public verification key, role, federation and model binding, and round-bound update proof are valid and unrevoked. Deny unknown, impersonated, expired, replayed, wrong-role, wrong-round, wrong-model, wrong-update, or unattested participants before update acceptance.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns federation participant enrollment, attestation, revocation, role, model and round binding, update-digest proof, replay prevention, and admission of the exact update to the exact round. It does not prove the authorized client is benign.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-008.003 decides who may submit which update; AID-H-008.001 protects accepted contributions from individual inspection.
Round admission and contribution confidentiality are independent requirements.

AID-H-008.003 rejects unknown, replayed, wrong-round, or unattested submitters; AID-H-008.002 mitigates malicious or outlier influence among updates that passed admission.
Identity assurance does not establish statistical safety.

AID-H-008.003 applies federated-learning-specific participant, model, round, and update binding; AID-H-004.003 supplies general peer identity, message integrity, replay, and task-protocol controls.
Generic secure communication does not decide federated round membership.

controls.name: Hardware Root of Trust & Secure Boot
controls.description_text: Establish and locally verify a hardware-rooted measured or verified boot chain for AI compute hosts, accelerator servers, and control nodes. Anchor trust in immutable or firmware keys; require approved signatures or measurements for firmware, UEFI, shim, bootloader, kernel, and boot-critical components; and bind the accepted state to host identity, firmware version, measurements, and versioned boot policy. Unauthorized startup components must fail locally.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns local hardware-rooted secure or measured boot validity for the host and boot-critical chain. It does not perform fresh remote cluster admission or manage vulnerability patch rollout.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-009.001 establishes and locally enforces the trusted boot state; AID-H-003.004 remotely verifies fresh hardware and firmware evidence and makes the cluster or workload admission decision.
Local boot validity is evidence consumed by the remote admission gate.

AID-H-009.001 validates that boot components satisfy the current approved policy; AID-H-009.002 discovers vulnerabilities and manages firmware or driver patch rollout and rollback.
Secure boot verifies authorized versions but does not decide when those versions are obsolete.

controls.name: Accelerator Firmware & Driver Patch Management
controls.description_text: This sub-technique covers the operational lifecycle management for the software that runs directly on the AI hardware. It includes processes for monitoring for vulnerabilities in firmware and drivers for GPUs, TPUs, and other accelerators, and applying security patches in a timely, controlled manner to prevent exploitation of known vulnerabilities.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns vulnerability monitoring, inventory, testing, staged rollout, rollback, and evidence for accelerator firmware and driver security updates.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-009.002 manages which firmware and driver versions should be deployed; AID-H-009.001 verifies that the boot chain loads only policy-approved components.
Patch lifecycle and boot enforcement are separate controls.

AID-H-009.002 remediates vulnerable firmware and drivers; AID-H-003.004 admits or rejects the current measured state at the cluster boundary.
Admission can block an unpatched node but does not perform the patch.

AID-H-009.002 owns accelerator firmware and driver remediation; AID-H-003.010 owns remediation of deployed AI application and platform software such as inference servers, orchestrators, SDKs, MCP components, and container images.
The controls use different advisories, compatibility matrices, rollout paths, and fleet evidence.

controls.name: Hardware Receipt Authenticity & Tamper-Evident Custody Verification
controls.description_text: Before an accelerator or supporting component is admitted to a build or cluster, verify physical identity, serial or lot record, manufacturer authenticity evidence where available, tamper seals, custody transitions, and receipt inspection against the exact asset. Quarantine any mismatch or unverifiable component.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns physical receipt authenticity, exact asset identity, tamper inspection, and custody-chain verification before hardware installation. It excludes supplier questionnaires and does not perform technical boot attestation or patch management.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-009.003 proves physical receipt and custody authenticity; AID-H-003.004 verifies measured hardware and firmware state and makes technical cluster admission decisions.
A valid shipment record does not establish the current runtime measurement.

AID-H-009.003 verifies the component's physical identity and custody before installation; AID-H-009.001 verifies its rooted boot chain after installation.
Custody and secure boot address different points in the hardware lifecycle.

controls.name: Accelerator Isolation & VRAM/KV-Cache Hygiene
controls.description_text: Prevent accelerator resources from crossing tenant or trust-zone boundaries unless the platform can independently prove an approved isolation and lifecycle-reset boundary. Serving-engine KV-cache eviction, process teardown, hardware partitioning, and provider-supported reset or disposable-worker replacement are valid mechanisms when their evidence is bound to the exact device and job transition. Framework allocator cleanup such as torch.cuda.empty_cache() is not secure zeroization and must never be accepted as proof.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns physical accelerator assignment, partition, reset, teardown, and low-level device-lifecycle evidence before reuse across tenants or trust zones. Framework allocator cleanup is not accepted as secure zeroization.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-009.004 protects physical accelerator and device-memory reuse; AID-H-027 protects logical inference caches through key binding, integrity, partitioning, expiry, and safe reuse policy.
Application cache eviction is not proof of hardware reset, and device reset does not validate cache keys.

AID-H-009.004 owns low-level device assignment and reset across trust zones; AID-H-032.002 owns broader cross-tenant serving-state isolation across batching, KV cache, allocators, buffers, and runtime workers.
Device lifecycle evidence is one layer of the complete serving-state boundary.

controls.name: Confidential Inference & Remote Attestation
controls.description_text: Run sensitive inference workloads inside attested confidential-computing environments that can protect model weights, prompts, embeddings, and serving-state caches from the host, hypervisor, and cloud operator. For modern LLM workloads this usually means VM-level TEEs such as Intel TDX or AMD SEV-SNP, paired with GPU confidential computing where accelerated inference is required, rather than assuming a classic SGX enclave can hold large model weights.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns confidential inference and key or data release based on fresh CPU, accelerator-set, runtime, interconnect, and supported topology attestation. Multi-GPU policy must distinguish Hopper and Blackwell profiles and must never infer encrypted interconnect or topology assurance from per-GPU attestation alone.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-009.005 protects plaintext inference inside an attested confidential runtime; AID-H-005.002 keeps supported computations on ciphertext and may use an enclave only for unsupported operations.
TEE confidentiality and homomorphic computation have different trust and performance assumptions.

AID-H-009.005 uses attestation as a preventive key and data release gate; AID-D-004.002 verifies and reports confidential-runtime attestation state as a detective integrity control.
Preventive secret release and independent runtime monitoring should not collapse into one decision path.

controls.name: Classifier-Free Guidance Hardening
controls.description_text:
A set of techniques focused on hardening the Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) mechanism in diffusion models.

What CFG does: CFG is a core component that steers image generation towards a text prompt, but adversaries can exploit high guidance scale values to force the model to generate harmful, unsafe, or out-of-distribution content.

The threat: High CFG scales can overpower built-in safety conditioning and negative prompts, effectively steering the diffusion model toward disallowed or high-risk generations.

Defense goal: These hardening techniques aim to control the CFG scale and its influence, preventing its misuse while preserving the model's creative capabilities.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns server-side policy enforcement and effective readback for Classifier-Free Guidance and related diffusion guider parameters when untrusted callers can influence them. It does not treat CFG, negative prompts, or risk heuristics as authoritative content filters.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-010 enforces diffusion-specific CFG and guider control surfaces at sampling time; AID-H-002.002 validates general inference prompts and request inputs.
A prompt that passes admission can still request an unsafe guidance configuration.

AID-H-010 owns CFG-specific diffusion semantics and safety constraints; AID-H-033.006 resolves and enforces the complete effective invocation configuration after gateway defaults, aliases, provider translation, and retries.
The gateway must preserve the specialized CFG policy but does not redefine it.

controls.name: Graph Data Sanitization & Provenance
controls.description_text: This sub-technique covers the data-centric defenses performed on a graph before training. It focuses on analyzing the graph's structure to identify and remove anomalous nodes or edges, and on incorporating provenance information (e.g., trust scores based on data sources) to down-weight the influence of less trusted parts of the graph during model training.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns pre-training graph-data sanitization, suspicious node or edge removal or down-weighting, and source-provenance weighting for graph inputs.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-011.001 changes or weights the graph data before training; AID-H-011.002 changes the model architecture, aggregation, regularization, and training policy to reduce structural fragility.
Data-centric and model-centric hardening can be deployed together but produce different evidence.

AID-H-011.001 removes or down-weights suspicious graph elements; AID-D-012.002 emits calibrated structure-feature anomaly findings without mutating the graph.
A detector finding may inform sanitization, but Detect must not silently delete graph data.

controls.name: Robust GNN Training & Architecture
controls.description_text: Select and train a GNN with policy-approved robust aggregation, regularization, edge pruning or weighting, or attention-based candidate architectures that reduce dependence on malicious neighbors and structurally fragile edges. Bind the exact graph schema, architecture, training policy, candidate digest, and comparative perturbation results, and block promotion when the declared robustness criteria are not met.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns model-centric GNN hardening through approved robust aggregation, regularization, edge weighting or pruning within training, attention architectures, comparative perturbation evidence, and promotion criteria.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-011.002 hardens how the GNN learns and aggregates neighbors; AID-H-011.001 sanitizes and weights graph data before training.
A robust model does not establish clean graph provenance, and sanitized data does not guarantee robust message passing.

AID-H-011.002 provides empirical model hardening and comparative perturbation results; AID-H-011.003 issues an exhaustive bounded certificate for an exact loaded state, graph, target, semantics, and candidate-edge universe.
Empirical robustness must not be reported as a formal certificate.

controls.name: Bounded GNN Structural Robustness Certification
controls.description_text: Produce an exact, replayable robustness certificate for a fixed loaded GNN state, model artifact, feature tensor, graph tensor, target node, explicitly declared directed or undirected semantics, and exact candidate-edge universe by exhaustively verifying every perturbation up to the requested radius. Bind the certificate to hashes of those exact inputs and issue it only for a radius that was fully enumerated; when the requested radius exceeds the policy safety cap, do not certify it, although a smaller fully verified radius may be reported explicitly.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns exact replayable certification of a fixed loaded GNN state against every structural perturbation within a fully enumerated radius, graph semantics, target node, feature and graph tensors, and candidate-edge universe. The certificate makes no claim outside that bound.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-011.003 proves a bounded formal property for exact inputs and perturbation universe; AID-H-011.002 empirically hardens and compares candidate architectures and training policies.
A certificate is narrower but stronger within its declared universe.

AID-H-011.003 exhaustively certifies every perturbation within a bounded universe; AID-D-012.001 measures candidate response to preregistered trigger and perturbation families.
Controlled trigger testing samples a threat contract and is not an exhaustive certificate.

AID-H-011.003 is the primary owner for exhaustive certification of a fixed GNN over an exact graph, target, candidate-edge universe, graph semantics, and structural radius; AID-H-015 owns other declared formal robustness properties and certification methods.
The same GNN structural certificate must not receive a second PASS under the generic certified-defense control.

controls.name: Robust Reward Function Engineering
controls.description_text: Directly engineer the reward function to be less exploitable. Define multiple positive goals, explicit negative penalties, and any optional shaping terms as one reviewed reward contract so that the agent cannot get a high score by doing something misaligned, unsafe, or trivial. Potential-based reward shaping is treated here as a reward-engineering method, not a separate control objective: it is acceptable only when the potential function, shaping wrapper, base reward, telemetry, and shortcut tests are versioned and verified together.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the explicit programmatic reward contract, including positive objectives, negative penalties, shaping terms, shortcut tests, versioning, and evidence that high reward corresponds to intended behavior.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-012.001 engineers explicit environment or task reward logic; AID-H-012.002 governs a learned reward function derived from preferences or demonstrations.
Programmatic reward design and learned signal calibration have different data and failure modes.

AID-H-012.001 prevents shortcuts in the reward function itself; AID-H-012.005 prevents policies from gaming learned reward models, AI judges, or programmatic verifiers during modern post-training.
A well-specified base reward does not eliminate evaluator-specific optimization exploits.

controls.name: Learned Reward-Signal Integrity & Calibration
controls.description_text: Protect training-specific integrity of learned reward functions built from preference pairs or expert demonstrations. Enforce signal-mode configuration, leakage-resistant train and evaluation partitions, reward-model calibration, abstention behavior, source-concentration checks, and adversarial validation.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns integrity and calibration of a learned reward signal derived from preference or demonstration data. It consumes label provenance but does not own the general labeling pipeline or the final policy's reward-gaming gate.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-012.002 trains, calibrates, and validates the learned reward signal; AID-H-002.005 proves provenance and integrity of the preference pairs, labels, or demonstrations supplied to it.
Trusted labels are necessary inputs but do not prove reward-model calibration.

AID-H-012.002 governs the learned reward model as a predictive signal; AID-H-012.005 tests whether the optimizing policy exploits that reward model or verifier.
A calibrated evaluator can still contain shortcuts that a policy discovers under optimization pressure.

controls.name: RL Behavioral Promotion Validation in Isolated Environments
controls.description_text: Before an RL policy is promoted, execute the exact candidate in a representative isolated environment and evaluate how reward was earned across the complete policy-defined episode population. Block promotion when behavior violates action, resource, safety, or task-outcome constraints even if aggregate reward is high.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns pre-release behavioral promotion validation of an exact RL candidate over complete policy-defined episodes in an isolated environment. It does not build the generic sandbox or perform production detection.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-012.003 validates the candidate's complete behavior and side effects in representative episodes; AID-H-012.005 focuses on gaming of reward models, judges, and verifiers.
Reward gaming is one failure class inside broader behavioral promotion validation.

AID-H-012.003 blocks unsafe RL candidates before release; AID-D-013 detects reward and policy manipulation from observed reward streams and trajectories.
Promotion validation and operational detection use different populations and outcomes.

controls.name: Secure Reward Signal Integrity & Transport
controls.description_text: Protect the integrity and authenticity of the reward signal itself. In many real systems, the reward is computed by an external service (simulation backend, telemetry service, rules arbiter). If an attacker can tamper with that reward in transit, the agent will learn a malicious or useless policy. This subtechnique treats the reward channel like a critical security surface: mutually authenticated transport plus cryptographic signing of the reward payload.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns authenticity, integrity, freshness, and service identity for externally computed reward payloads and their transport before the reward is consumed for learning.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-H-012.004 protects the reward value from transport or service tampering; AID-H-012.001 determines whether the reward function itself encodes the intended objective.
An authentic reward can still be badly designed, and a sound reward is useless if attackers can alter it in transit.

AID-H-012.004 is the primary owner for an externally computed reward payload's producer identity, integrity, freshness, and learning-consumption binding; AID-H-004.005 supplies a protocol-independent signed-envelope primitive when intermediaries break transport trust.
The same signed reward evidence must not earn a second PASS under the generic message control.
