controls.name: Query-Document Semantic Relevance Anomaly Detection
controls.description_text: Re-score the complete live query-to-chunk top-k with a pinned cross-encoder or other model that is separate from the retriever's bi-encoder/vector score, and alert on semantically off-topic retrievals that may indicate poisoning or false entry injection.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns semantic relevance anomaly findings by independently re-scoring the complete live query-to-chunk top-k with a pinned model separate from the retriever's primary score.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-D-014.002 detects off-topic or unexpectedly weak query-to-chunk relevance; AID-D-014.001 detects malicious instructions and payloads inside retrieved content.
Relevance and content safety are independent properties.

AID-D-014.002 evaluates semantic fit between the query and each chunk; AID-D-014.003 evaluates source identity, ordered population completeness, diversity, concentration, duplicates, and registry membership.
A highly relevant result can still come from an unapproved or over-concentrated source.

controls.name: Retrieval Source Provenance, Diversity & Coverage Monitoring
controls.description_text: Compare the ordered top-k retrieval population with an authenticated gateway completeness record and versioned source registry. Detect missing or unregistered provenance, minimum-k shortfall, collection-coverage gaps, duplicate or reordered chunks, and calibrated source-diversity or concentration violations. Calibrate thresholds per query class, route, and index on a versioned benign and adversarial corpus; the framework publishes no universal concentration percentage. Missing provenance, unsupported source identity, incomplete population, and unreadable or unverifiable policy must remain explicit and must not be reported as clean retrieval. This detector emits findings; it does not suppress or re-rank sources.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns ordered top-k retrieval provenance, registry membership, minimum-count coverage, collection coverage, duplicate and reorder detection, and calibrated source-diversity or concentration findings. It does not suppress, re-rank, sign, or admit sources.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-D-014.003 verifies source and population properties of the retrieval set; AID-D-014.002 measures semantic relevance of query-to-chunk pairs.
Provenance and coverage do not establish relevance, and relevance does not establish authorized source identity or complete retrieval.

AID-D-014.003 emits provenance, diversity, and coverage findings; AID-H-020 enforces signed chunk integrity, source authorization, and retrieval-time hygiene.
The detector observes and reports the retrieval population, while Harden decides whether it may enter context.

controls.name: High-Risk Approval Bypass & HITL Activity Detection
controls.description_text: Detect missing, invalid, expired, mismatched, replayed, or anomalous human-approval records around high-risk agent actions, and monitor HITL request, decision, escalation, release, and execution activity for unattended or abusive patterns. Correlate the signed approval, authenticated operator, exact action digest, policy version, and canonical event chain against the execution record; this control never authorizes or executes the action.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns telemetry correlation, signed approval-record validation, HITL activity analytics, and findings for missing, invalid, expired, mismatched, replayed, unattended, or abusive high-risk approval lifecycles. It never authorizes, unlocks, or executes the action.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-D-015 independently detects bypass, replay, mismatch, expiry, and anomalous approval activity; AID-H-018.003 validates the exact high-impact action and issues the canonical runtime approval or denial receipt.
The detector must remain independent of the gate whose failures it is intended to find.

AID-D-015 detects violations and anomalies in the observed HITL event chain; AID-M-006.003 defines the canonical escalation topology, event fields, producer obligations, and reconciliation contract.
The Model control specifies expected evidence, while Detect owns production findings when that evidence is missing or inconsistent.

controls.name: Agent Graph Baseline & New-Agent Discovery
controls.description_text: Discover previously unseen agent identities and new communication edges by comparing authenticated service-mesh and registry observations with a versioned approved agent graph.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns unknown or newly emergent agent identity and communication-edge discovery against a versioned approved graph. It does not score reputation or classify drift within identities already registered.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-D-016.001 discovers identities and edges absent from the approved graph; AID-D-011.003 detects replica, namespace, workload, and image-lineage drift for identities already registered.
A new identity is a rogue-agent discovery candidate rather than an ordinary registered-population variance.

AID-D-016.001 establishes that an identity or edge is new or unknown; AID-D-016.002 combines that and other security signals into reputation and escalation evidence.
Discovery is one input to scoring, not the containment recommendation itself.

AID-D-016.001 discovers active or observed agent identities and communication edges from runtime graph behavior; AID-M-001.006 discovers organization-owned internal AI endpoints from private-network and control-plane scope.
A reachable service endpoint is not necessarily an active agent node, and agent behavior can reveal identities that endpoint enumeration misses.

controls.name: Reputation Scoring & Containment Escalation Signals
controls.description_text: Score agent reputation continuously using signals such as unknown identity, signature failures, abnormal tool usage, and egress anomalies, then emit auditable escalation recommendations when thresholds are crossed.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns deduplicated, time-windowed, auditable agent reputation scoring and escalation evidence. It stops at scoring and recommendation and does not execute quarantine, eviction, or restoration.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-D-016.002 scores reputation from discovery and other detector signals; AID-D-016.001 owns the specific unknown-identity and new-edge finding.
A new identity can inform reputation but must not be treated as the complete risk score.

AID-D-016.002 emits reputation and containment-escalation evidence; AID-I-003 applies quarantine, throttling, or safe-mode containment.
A threshold crossing is a recommendation until an authorized Isolate control enforces it.

controls.name: AI Detection SLO & Alert-Coverage Measurement
controls.description_text:
Establish measurable detection service-level objectives for AI and agentic systems by tracking how quickly observable anomalies become alerts, how quickly alerts are acknowledged and triaged, and how much of the alert queue is investigated across agent sessions, tool calls, memory writes, retrieval events, inference gateways, and high-risk actions.

Primary metrics: detection_latency measures anomaly observed to alert created; acknowledgement_latency measures alert created to human acknowledged; triage_latency measures human acknowledged to triage completed; investigation_ratio measures triage-completed non-duplicate eligible alerts divided by the complete non-duplicate eligible population.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns end-to-end detection service-level measurement for anomaly-to-alert latency, alert acknowledgement, triage completion, and investigation coverage over complete bounded alert cohorts. It does not own individual alert semantics, telemetry collection, or posture SLOs.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-D-017 measures service-level speed and investigation coverage from observation through triage; AID-D-005.010 measures whether sensors and the telemetry pipeline remain healthy and complete.
Healthy telemetry is necessary but does not prove alerts are timely, acknowledged, or investigated.

AID-D-017 measures operational latency and alert-queue handling coverage; AID-D-018 measures scenario-level recall, precision, false positives, errors, abstentions, and detector coverage.
Fast triage of an alert does not prove the detector finds the right attacks, and high recall does not prove timely operations.

AID-D-017 owns detection and investigation SLOs; AID-M-005.002 owns secure-configuration posture criteria and build or release gates.
Detection service quality and configuration posture are separate operational objectives.

controls.name: Production AI-Security Detection Efficacy & Scenario-Coverage Validation
controls.description_text: Continuously validate the efficacy and scenario coverage of the exact AI-security detectors deployed in production by replaying signed benign and attack scenarios through their real observation paths, measuring segmented recall, precision, false-positive rate, errors, and abstentions, and binding results to detector versions, digests, policies, and a complete eligible inventory.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns cross-detector production-path efficacy and fleet-wide scenario coverage by replaying signed benign and attack scenarios through real observation paths and measuring segmented recall, precision, false positives, errors, abstentions, and complete detector-by-scenario coverage.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-D-018 determines whether deployed detectors identify required scenarios with acceptable efficacy; AID-D-005.002 determines whether rule assets are packaged, deployed, routed, and technically healthy.
Execution health is not semantic detection efficacy.

AID-D-018 measures detector correctness and scenario coverage; AID-D-017 measures detection, acknowledgement, triage latency, and investigation coverage.
Detector quality and operational response service levels require separate result sets.

AID-D-018 validates the production security detectors and their real observation paths; AID-M-008 benchmarks the protected model or agent against adversarial behavior before or alongside release.
The detector under test and the protected AI system under test are different assets.

AID-D-018 validates scenario efficacy for the production detector fleet; AID-D-008 owns the design, training, calibration, and serving of its fusion detector.
The efficacy control may test fusion output but does not retrain or operate the fusion model.

controls.name: Container-Based Isolation
controls.description_text: Utilizes container technologies like Docker or Kubernetes to package and run AI workloads in isolated user-space environments. This approach provides process and filesystem isolation and allows for resource management and network segmentation.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns container-level process, filesystem, privilege, resource, and network isolation for AI workloads that can accept a shared host-kernel boundary. It does not claim the stronger kernel or hardware separation of a microVM or user-space-kernel sandbox.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-001.001 uses conventional containers and a shared host kernel; AID-I-001.002 adds a microVM, user-space kernel, WASM capability boundary, or lower-level OS sandbox.
Choose AID-I-001.002 when untrusted code or workload sensitivity requires stronger-than-container isolation. A hardened container alone does not satisfy that stronger boundary.

controls.name: MicroVM & Low-Level Sandboxing
controls.description_text: Employs lightweight Virtual Machines (MicroVMs), user-space kernel sandboxes, and OS-level sandbox primitives to provide a stronger isolation boundary than traditional containers. This is critical for running untrusted code, browser-driven agent tools, or highly sensitive AI workloads where shared-kernel escape, filesystem writes, and uncontrolled network egress must be constrained in layers.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns stronger-than-container execution isolation through microVMs, user-space kernels, WASM capability runtimes, or OS sandbox primitives. It defines isolation strength and permitted host interaction, but not per-invocation freshness, deterministic teardown, or artifact-analysis verdicts.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-001.002 provides a stronger kernel or hardware isolation boundary; AID-I-001.001 uses conventional shared-kernel containers.
Use the container control when its threat model is sufficient, and this control when shared-kernel escape or hostile code requires a stronger boundary.

AID-I-001.002 selects and verifies runtime isolation strength; AID-I-001.003 creates a fresh sandbox for one tool invocation and proves teardown.
A microVM can be long-lived, and a single-use sandbox can consume different approved runtime profiles. Isolation strength and one-shot lifecycle are separate controls.

controls.name: Ephemeral Single-Use Sandboxes for Tools
controls.description_text: Run each high-risk tool invocation in a fresh, single-use sandbox instance and destroy that instance immediately after the invocation completes, fails, or times out. The unique control value is per-invocation freshness and guaranteed teardown: no reused workspace, no inherited filesystem residue, no lingering process, and no persistent foothold for a compromised tool.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns per-invocation sandbox freshness, one-shot execution, deterministic teardown, lease revocation, and evidence that no workspace, process, or residue survived the tool call. It delegates isolation strength and egress-policy definition to their canonical controls.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-001.003 owns the single-use lifecycle; AID-I-001.002 owns the microVM, user-space-kernel, WASM, or OS-level isolation profile.
This control binds an approved profile to one invocation but does not independently establish the strength of that profile.

AID-I-001.003 creates and destroys the one-shot sandbox; AID-I-001.004 defines and independently enforces its outbound network policy.
A teardown receipt does not prove default-deny egress, and an egress policy does not prove that the invocation used a fresh workspace or was destroyed.

AID-I-001.003 provides one-shot execution and teardown for a tool invocation; AID-I-001.005 detonates an artifact across a declared case population and emits attested raw behavioral observations.
Detonation consumes sandbox lifecycle evidence but has a separate artifact-analysis population and output; ordinary ephemeral tool execution is not a behavioral-analysis result.

controls.name: Sandbox Network Egress Restrictions
controls.description_text: Restrict outbound network destinations for sandboxed executions with default-deny egress policy and narrow allowlists to reduce exfiltration, callback traffic, and lateral movement after code execution.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns named sandbox egress policies, destination allowlists, externally enforced proxies or network controls, and bypass testing for sandboxed execution. Other controls may bind to an egress-policy reference, but they do not inherit proof that its effective network path is enforced.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-001.004 restricts outbound network paths; AID-I-001.003 owns fresh single-use sandbox creation and teardown.
A sandbox may be ephemeral without default-deny egress, and egress restriction can apply to a reused or long-lived runtime; both properties require separate evidence.

AID-I-001.004 owns the reusable sandbox egress-policy object and its external enforcement; AID-H-019.003 owns admission and observation export for a browser runtime.
The browser control binds to this policy but does not redefine the allowlist, proxy enforcement, or network-bypass tests.

AID-I-001.004 is the primary owner for default-deny egress and bypass resistance of sandboxed execution; AID-I-002.002 owns governed connectivity from AI workloads to external MaaS, SaaS, APIs, callbacks, relays, and cross-organization agents.
When a sandbox calls an external AI service, identical network-policy evidence may be reused, but the same default-deny enforcement must not receive two PASS outcomes; AID-I-002.002 must additionally prove its external endpoint, transport, and mediation population.

controls.name: Safe Ephemeral Detonation & Attested Raw Observation Reporting
controls.description_text: Detonate every policy-designated executable artifact, including scripts, binaries, container images, plugins, and model-loader candidates, against a complete versioned case population inside a short-lived deny-by-default microVM or equivalent boundary. The detonation receives no production credentials or host-write path, exposes only policy-declared instrumented egress, and exports only attested raw behavioral observations plus measurement metadata bound to the artifact digest, analyzer image, sandbox profile, execution receipt, case population, and policy version. Unsupported artifacts, missing telemetry, suspected escape, or absent destruction and residue evidence leave the analysis unresolved and must not be treated as evidence that the artifact is benign.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns safe artifact-detonation orchestration, complete case execution, attested raw behavioral observations, anti-analysis findings, and observation metadata. It does not claim that one run proves an artifact benign and does not issue a promotion credential.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-001.005 owns artifact detonation and raw observation completeness; AID-I-001.003 owns single-use sandbox creation, teardown, lease revocation, and residue checks.
Detonation must consume the authenticated destruction and no-residue receipt before closing a case, but it adds a separate analysis population and attested observation result.

AID-I-001.005 emits attested raw dynamic-analysis observations; AID-H-031.003 combines dynamic, static, and provenance evidence to decide artifact promotion.
A detonation finding is evidence for the promotion gate, not the release decision itself.

controls.name: Internal AI Network Segmentation
controls.description_text:
Implement network segmentation and microsegmentation strategies to isolate AI systems and their internal components (e.g., training environments, model serving endpoints, data stores, agent control planes) from general corporate networks and other critical IT/OT systems.

Internal Communication Controls
Enforces strict internal communication rules through firewalls, security groups, and network policies to limit lateral movement and reduce the internal blast radius of a compromise.

Agent Backend Isolation
This also isolates high-privilege agent backends (e.g. orchestration layers with access to credentials, vector DBs, or model registries) from lower-trust, user-facing inference frontends, so that a compromised public-facing agent cannot laterally move into data-rich components.

A2A applicability: The measured internal reachability population includes every agent-to-agent gateway or listener, broker topic or queue, direct peer edge, discovery-advertised endpoint, callback, and relay crossing an internal trust-zone boundary. Apply the allow/deny graph to authenticated workload identities and exact peer routes, not only user-facing service ports.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns segmentation and measured reachability among organization-controlled internal AI components, trust zones, environments, agent listeners, broker topics, and peer routes. It does not govern connections to remote third-party, SaaS, or cross-organization services.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-002.001 segments internal organization-controlled networks and components; AID-I-002.002 governs connections from the AI system to external services and cross-organization agent endpoints.
Classify the path by the destination trust and administrative boundary, not merely by whether the endpoint uses a private address or encrypted transport.

controls.name: Secure External AI Service Connectivity
controls.description_text:
Applies strict network path control, transport security, policy mediation, and monitoring specifically to connections originating from the AI system and targeting external services, particularly third-party or Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) foundation model APIs. Aims to prevent data exfiltration, Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks, and abuse of external dependencies. This also prevents prompt-injected agents from exfiltrating secrets or invoking arbitrary external services; they can only call approved upstreams through a governed path.

A2A applicability: The measured external reachability population includes every remote or third-party agent endpoint, Agent Card-derived route, callback, relay, broker bridge, and cross-organization peer connection. Default-deny unknown destinations and independently read back the effective egress and inbound exposure for the complete endpoint population.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns default-deny network path control, transport security, mediation, and effective-reachability verification for external MaaS, SaaS, API, callback, relay, broker-bridge, and cross-organization agent connections. It does not define internal microsegmentation between organization-controlled components.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-002.002 governs external and cross-organization service connectivity; AID-I-002.001 segments internal organization-controlled AI systems and trust zones.
A privately addressed provider route can still be external by ownership and trust boundary, while an Internet-routable organization-owned endpoint may remain part of the internal administrative population.

AID-I-002.002 owns external-service endpoint, transport, mediation, and reachability controls for the applicable AI-workload population; AID-I-001.004 is the primary owner for default-deny egress and bypass tests of sandboxed executions.
For an external call originating inside a sandbox, reuse the sandbox network evidence without scoring the identical enforcement twice, and evaluate the additional external-service identity and mediation requirements here.

controls.name: Detection-Driven Quarantine & Safe-Mode Downgrade
controls.description_text:
Convert high-confidence detector findings, health signals, trust-state demotions, or analyst-approved SOAR decisions into bounded quarantine, safe-mode, or hard-containment actions. This sub-technique owns signed finding intake, target resolution, containment playbook execution, degraded-mode state, escalation from soft throttling to hard containment, and post-action verification.

A2A containment: Disable or quarantine the contained agent's peer registrations, discovery advertisements, message routes, delegated leases, and pending cross-agent work so isolation covers inter-agent execution paths as well as user-facing endpoints.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns reversible detection-driven quarantine, safe-mode downgrade, hard-containment playbook execution, target resolution, and post-action verification. It consumes signed findings or decisions and does not compute anomaly scores or perform long-term eviction.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-003.001 applies reversible detection-driven quarantine or safe mode; AID-E-002 terminates confirmed-compromised active execution and revokes execution leases.
Escalate to E-002 when continued runtime existence is no longer acceptable; do not report a quarantine state as process or pod eviction.

AID-I-003.001 contains a resolved target through quarantine or degraded mode; AID-I-005 issues and enforces a last-resort system-wide or tenant-wide halt.
A target-scoped safe mode can be an input to escalation, but it does not satisfy global halt coverage or restart-gate evidence.

controls.name: Identity, Session & API Rate-Limit Throttling
controls.description_text: Apply atomic admission-control throttles at the API gateway or application edge for authenticated principals, tenants, sessions, API keys, and low-trust or unauthenticated callers. For AI endpoints exposed to untrusted clients, consume trusted bot or abuse signals to apply additional bounded restrictions to suspicious traffic, including correlated rotating sources where the deployed service supports them. Preserve the base identity allowance when adaptive restrictions change. This sub-technique owns identity binding, base trust-tier limits, server-derived admission costs, quota enforcement and bounded adaptive responses; it does not require a custom ML detector.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns request-admission throttling by principal, tenant, session, API key or trust tier, and additional restrictions on a bounded suspicious traffic set, at the gateway or application edge. It consumes trusted bot or abuse findings without owning their detection or attribution. It does not enforce cumulative GPU, CPU, token, tool-call, retry, concurrency or spend budgets and does not decide the disposition of one high-risk action.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-003.002 limits request admission rates by identity or session; AID-I-003.003 limits cumulative resource, token, concurrency, retry, tool-call, and spend consumption.
Expensive low-frequency abuse can pass a request-rate limit but exceed a resource budget, while a high request rate may be throttled before cumulative compute becomes abnormal.

AID-I-003.002 throttles a stream of API requests; AID-I-003.004 blocks, defers, reroutes, or escalates one proposed high-risk agent action before side effects.
A per-identity rate limit does not determine whether an individual action is safe to execute.

controls.name: Resource, Token & Spend Budget Throttling
controls.description_text: Throttle cumulative resource consumption when suspicious tenants, sessions, users, agents, or API keys exceed GPU, CPU, token, tool-call, retry, concurrency, or spend budgets. This sub-technique owns multi-dimensional quota policy, server-side usage accounting, Kubernetes resource clamps, budget ledgers, and quota evidence.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns multi-dimensional cumulative resource and spend budgets, server-side accounting, quota ledgers, platform resource clamps, and quota evidence. It controls expensive low-frequency or recursive consumption rather than only request arrival rate.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-003.003 throttles cumulative compute, token, tool-call, retry, concurrency, and spend consumption; AID-I-003.002 throttles request admission by identity, tenant, session, API key, or trust tier.
Both may apply to one caller, but they measure and enforce different populations and cannot share a PASS result.

controls.name: High-Risk Agent Action Containment
controls.description_text: Contain high-risk agent actions at the dispatcher or orchestration boundary before irreversible side effects occur.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns incident-time or elevated-risk disposition of one proposed agent action through block, defer, safer re-plan, approved routing, or required human approval before side effects. It consumes upstream authorization, trust-state, goal-integrity, or anomaly signals and does not define preventive capability authorization.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-003.004 contains an action after live risk signals require a response; AID-H-018 defines and enforces the preventive runtime authorization and capability boundary.
An action can be authorized under normal policy yet contained because incident-time risk changed, and containment does not replace the baseline authorization decision.

AID-I-003.004 decides the disposition of one high-risk proposed action; AID-I-003.002 throttles request volume for a caller or session.
A low-rate action can still require containment because of its effect, while a high-rate request stream may be throttled without any individual action being high impact.

Containment can require fresh high-impact approval and consumes the canonical H-018.003 receipt; it does not implement another approval authority or count that approval twice. Containment owns the separate risk-triggered disposition and dispatcher fence.

controls.name: Runtime Context Isolation & Hygiene
controls.description_text: Enforces strict boundaries and hygiene for volatile working memory (RAM/Redis). Prevents cross-session/cross-tenant context bleed, limits the temporal blast radius of prompt injections (via windowing/resets), and prevents resource exhaustion (DoS/cost burn) via size/token ceilings and TTL.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns isolation and hygiene of volatile active context and working memory by session and tenant, including bounded size, token ceilings, TTL, resets, and fail-closed serialization. It does not partition persistent memory, govern phase-specific secret demotion, or validate summary transformations.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.001 isolates volatile session working context; AID-I-004.002 partitions persistent vector, RAG, and long-term memory by tenant and trust tier.
A Redis or in-memory session boundary does not establish durable namespace isolation, and persistent partitioning does not enforce active-context size, TTL, or reset hygiene.

AID-I-004.001 separates and limits active context by session or tenant; AID-I-004.007 removes or demotes secrets and privileged intermediate state at verified task-phase transitions within a live session.
General context isolation does not prove that no-longer-needed sensitive values were replaced when the task moved to a new phase.

AID-I-004.001 owns active-context boundaries and hygiene; AID-I-004.008 validates the security integrity of a summarization or compaction transformation.
A bounded context window does not prove that a generated summary preserved constraints, provenance, or secret-removal requirements.

AID-I-004.001 owns steady-state isolation, size, TTL, reset, and serialization enforcement for volatile runtime context stores; AID-H-017.004 owns the application architecture that avoids retained cross-task state and reloads trusted mission objectives.
Store isolation and TTL receive their outcome here even when a stateless design references the same runtime evidence.

controls.name: Persistent Memory Partitioning (Trust & Tenant Isolation)
controls.description_text: Defines structural isolation for long-term memory (Vector DB/RAG). Uses namespaces/collections partitioned by tenant and trust tier, and enforces retrieval authorization via a centralized policy decision (never by agent self-assertion).

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns structural partitioning and retrieval authorization for persistent memory, vector stores, and RAG namespaces by tenant and trust tier. It does not define whether a candidate write is eligible for a trust tier or govern volatile active context.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.002 isolates persistent long-term memory namespaces; AID-I-004.001 isolates volatile session and tenant working context.
Persistent partitioning and active-context hygiene have different stores, lifetimes, evidence populations, and failure modes.

AID-I-004.002 enforces persistent namespace and retrieval isolation; AID-M-002.004 defines the provenance, write-eligibility, trust-tier, evidence, and namespace metadata contract.
The Model control publishes which state and namespace a write should receive; this control makes that partition and retrieval boundary effective at runtime.

controls.name: Cryptographic Memory Integrity (Signed Write/Verify Read)
controls.description_text: Establishes an end-to-end integrity loop for persistent memory: a controlled writer issues signed records (content-hash + metadata + key id), and an integrity-first loader verifies signatures and hashes before any content can re-enter agent context. This prevents direct-to-DB poisoning/tampering and forces memory provenance to be verifiable.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns cryptographic integrity of persistent memory records after an authorized write by signing canonical content and metadata and verifying signatures and hashes before readmission to context. It does not decide who may request a protected write or whether the candidate content should be promoted.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.003 proves cryptographic integrity after an authorized persistent-memory write; AID-I-004.006 enforces who may write protected file-backed identity and state resources.
A valid signature does not establish write authorization, and OS-level write protection does not prove that an accepted record's content and metadata remained intact.

AID-I-004.003 verifies signed memory integrity; AID-I-004.004 controls transactional promotion from quarantined to trusted memory.
An intact record can still be untrusted or ineligible, while a promotion receipt must bind to integrity evidence rather than replace it.

controls.name: Transactional Promotion Gates (Quarantine -> Trusted)
controls.description_text: Implements a strict state machine and atomic promotion workflow for high-risk memory writes. Items routed into quarantine cannot influence agent behavior until reviewed and promoted. Promotion must be transactional, auditable, and typically re-signed as trusted. Aligns with trust-tiered memory write-gates (e.g., trusted/probation/quarantined).

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the durable memory state machine and transactional promotion of an exact quarantined write into trusted memory, including review binding, compare-and-swap state transition, re-signing, audit evidence, and idempotent publication. It does not define the upstream eligibility contract or authorize transient peer data to persist automatically.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.004 executes the runtime quarantine-to-trusted promotion; AID-M-002.004 defines the write-eligibility, provenance, trust-tier, evidence, and namespace contract consumed by that gate.
A recommended trust tier is not a promotion result, and a promotion gate must not invent eligibility metadata outside the signed contract.

AID-I-004.004 promotes an approved write into durable trusted memory; AID-I-004.009 promotes a bounded peer-message projection only into transient active context as peer-untrusted data.
A peer context-promotion receipt never authorizes persistence, trust-tier elevation, or durable-memory promotion.

AID-I-004.004 decides and records durable trust promotion; AID-I-004.003 signs and verifies persistent-memory content and metadata integrity.
Promotion must consume integrity evidence, but integrity alone does not determine that the record is eligible for trusted use.

controls.name: Memory TTL, Staleness Decay & Forced Forgetting
controls.description_text: Apply policy-defined trust decay, re-validation, downgrade, and deletion to persistent memory so stale records do not remain implicitly trusted. Bind each decision to the record version, tenant, trust tier, freshness metadata, retention policy, and deletion or downgrade evidence.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns policy-defined trust decay, revalidation, downgrade, retention, deletion, and forced forgetting for persistent memory records and their derived replicas, indexes, summaries, and caches. Missing cleanup evidence or an unreadable record population leaves the lifecycle action unresolved.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.005 governs persistent-record TTL, staleness, revalidation, downgrade, and deletion; AID-I-004.001 governs volatile session-context TTL, size, resets, and tenant isolation.
The same duration policy may inform both, but persistent deletion and volatile context expiry require separate populations and receipts.

AID-I-004.005 removes or downgrades persistent records because of retention or staleness; AID-I-004.007 demotes secrets and privileged context when a live task changes phase.
Phase transition is not the same event as persistent-record expiry, and one control's cleanup evidence does not satisfy the other.

controls.name: Agent Identity & Persistent State File Write Protection
controls.description_text: Protect high-trust, file-backed agent identity and persistent state, such as logical identity, primary-memory, and agent-configuration resources, from unauthorized writes that could survive skill removal, restart, or redeployment. Enforce OS-level write restrictions, a controlled-writer path, immutable baselines, reviewed diffs, rollback, and tamper evidence against the complete protected-file inventory.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns write authorization and enforcement at protected file-backed agent identity, primary-memory, and configuration surfaces through OS restrictions, a controlled writer, immutable baselines, reviewed diffs, rollback, and tamper evidence. Database-backed and vector-backed memory use the other AID-I-004 controls.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.006 controls who may write protected file-backed identity and state; AID-I-004.003 proves cryptographic integrity of persistent-memory records after an authorized write.
Write authorization and post-write integrity are separate claims and require separate enforcement and verification evidence.

AID-I-004.006 enforces the protected file-write boundary; AID-H-018.007 determines whether an installed skill may request that capability under its permission manifest.
A skill permission is an input to the file control, not proof that the exact write was allowed, mediated, or durably recorded.

controls.name: Task-Bounded Context Segmentation & Secret Demotion
controls.description_text: Segment active context by task phase within a live session. At each verified phase transition, replace raw secrets, privileged intermediate results, temporary credentials, and internal-only instructions with short-lived scoped handles, redacted summaries, or non-retrievable references when the next phase no longer requires the original value. Bind the transition evidence to the task, old and new phase, policy version, affected context fields, and demotion result.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns intra-session task-phase segmentation and demotion of raw secrets, privileged intermediate results, temporary credentials, and internal-only instructions into scoped handles, redacted summaries, or non-retrievable references when the next phase no longer needs them.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.007 changes sensitive context at a verified phase transition within one session; AID-I-004.001 isolates and limits the session's volatile context as a whole.
Session isolation does not prove that a secret was demoted when its task need ended, while phase demotion does not establish cross-session or cross-tenant isolation.

AID-I-004.007 demotes sensitive active context because the live task changed phase; AID-I-004.005 expires, downgrades, or deletes persistent records under retention and staleness policy.
The triggers, stores, evidence populations, and cleanup semantics are different even when both reduce retained sensitive state.

AID-I-004.007 decides which context must be removed or demoted at a phase transition; AID-I-004.008 validates the security integrity of the summary or compaction transformation used to represent remaining context.
A valid compaction does not decide phase need, and a phase policy does not prove that a generated summary preserved constraints or removed secrets correctly.

controls.name: Context Summary & Compaction Integrity
controls.description_text: At each context summarization, compaction, or distillation event, validate the compacted output before it can re-enter active or persistent context. Preserve security-critical constraints and provenance, detect carried-forward poisoned content, prevent raw-secret retention, and bind evidence to the input and output digests, model revision, transformation policy, and verification result. When the verifier cannot run or does not support the input, keep the summary quarantined.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns validation of each context summarization, compaction, or distillation transformation before its output re-enters active or persistent context. It preserves security-critical constraints and provenance, detects carried-forward poison, rejects raw-secret retention, and keeps unsupported or unverifiable summaries quarantined.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.008 validates the compression transformation and its output; AID-I-004.001 isolates and limits the surrounding volatile session context.
Context hygiene does not prove summary fidelity or safety, and a valid summary does not establish session or tenant isolation.

AID-I-004.008 checks whether transformed context is safe and faithful; AID-I-004.005 governs persistent-record retention, staleness, downgrade, and deletion.
Compaction is not a retention receipt, and deleting or expiring a record does not validate any summary derived from it.

AID-I-004.008 verifies a summary or compaction output; AID-I-004.007 decides which secrets and privileged intermediate state must be demoted at a task-phase transition.
When summarization implements demotion, both the phase decision and the transformation validation remain independently necessary.

controls.name: Peer-Agent Message Context Quarantine & Promotion
controls.description_text: Keep every authenticated peer-agent message outside active and persistent model context until the exact received bytes pass transport-admission and content-validation controls and a trusted promotion service emits a single-use, work-scope-bound receipt for a bounded typed projection. Promoted content remains explicitly peer_untrusted data with no instruction, policy, credential, tool, or delegated-authority semantics. Missing, stale, unsupported, partially covered, or unverifiable evidence remains quarantined and is INSUFFICIENT_DATA or ERROR, never PASS.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns transient quarantine and active-context promotion for messages received from peer agents over A2A, custom agent protocols, gateways, relays, or sub-agent runtimes. It applies when a peer-message path exists and a trusted context assembler can enforce typed trust metadata. Promoted content remains peer-untrusted data with no instruction, policy, credential, tool, delegated-authority, or durable-persistence semantics.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-004.009 quarantines and promotes peer-message content into active context; AID-H-004.003 authenticates the peer, protects the channel and message, prevents replay, and authorizes the A2A task.
A transport-admission PASS is required input but does not authorize model-context admission or change peer content into trusted instructions.

AID-I-004.009 owns quarantine state and context admission; AID-H-002.002 validates the received bytes for schema, encoding, size, and prompt-injection risk.
Content validation is a required signed input, while this control decides whether a bounded projection can enter active context and with which trust semantics.

AID-I-004.009 promotes a bounded peer-message projection only into transient active context; AID-I-004.004 promotes an approved write into durable trusted memory.
A context-promotion receipt never authorizes persistence, trusted-memory status, or reuse beyond its bounded work scope.

AID-I-004.009 owns the peer-message quarantine and context-promotion state machine; AID-H-017.007 is an optional dual-LLM analysis mechanism for untrusted content.
The analyzer can supply evidence but does not own quarantine storage, promotion atomicity, trust metadata, or context-assembler enforcement.

controls.name: Emergency "Kill-Switch" / AI System Halt
controls.description_text: Establish and maintain a reliable, rapidly invokable mechanism to immediately halt, disable, or severely restrict the operation of an AI model or autonomous agent if it exhibits confirmed critical malicious behavior, behaves as a rogue agent (acts far outside its intended parameters in a harmful way), or if a severe, ongoing attack is detected and other containment measures are insufficient. This is a last-resort containment measure designed to prevent catastrophic harm or further compromise.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the authoritative emergency RUN, HALT, or severely restricted operating decision and its verified enforcement at every required inference and agent-loop boundary. It is a last-resort containment mechanism; it does not itself revoke credentials, terminate every runtime object, or delete durable application state.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-005 halts or severely restricts a complete system or tenant under an emergency decision; AID-I-003 applies bounded quarantine, degradation, throttling, or action containment to scoped targets.
Use I-003 when limited reversible containment is sufficient and I-005 when policy requires a last-resort halt with complete propagation and restart-gate evidence.

AID-I-005 publishes and enforces the emergency operating state; AID-E-002 terminates exact active processes, agent runs, execution leases, jobs, pods, and containers.
A HALT decision can block execution gates without proving that every live runtime object was terminated, so E-002 supplies the separate eviction receipt when required.

controls.name: Federated Client Quarantine & Exclusion
controls.description_text: Quarantine and exclude federated-learning clients whose cryptographically bound identities have been suspended or denied by an authoritative incident-response control plane. Enforce the deny decision at enrollment, client selection, update ingestion, training, retraining, and recovery/unlearning boundaries so a blocked participant cannot rejoin under the same identity or continue contributing cached updates.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns authoritative, identity-bound federated-client quarantine decisions, signed deny-state distribution, and exclusion enforcement at enrollment, selection, update ingestion, training, retraining, and recovery. Statistical clustering and reputation may nominate investigation candidates but cannot independently prove malice or authorize durable quarantine.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-006 excludes clients already named in a verified quarantine decision; AID-H-008.002 robustly aggregates updates from the accepted client population.
Byzantine-robust aggregation is not identity-bound eviction, and quarantine does not define how accepted updates are combined or made robust to residual outliers.

AID-I-006 produces and enforces the signed federated-client and update exclusion population; AID-R-001.002 consumes that population when building sanitized recovery-training inputs and validating a newly remediated model.
Recovery retraining must not recreate the quarantine decision, and successful exclusion does not prove that the replacement model passed remediation evaluation.

controls.name: Client-Side AI Execution Isolation
controls.description_text: This technique focuses on containing a compromised or malicious client-side model, preventing it from accessing sensitive data from other browser tabs, local application context, or the operating system. It addresses the security challenges of AI models that execute in untrusted environments like a user's web browser, Electron shell, hybrid mobile app, or native mobile runtime. This assumes the model or model runtime may already be tampered with or coerced (e.g. prompt-injected, modified weights, wrapped with hostile JS). The goal is not to "fix" the model but to strictly confine its blast radius using sandboxing, least capability, and controlled IPC.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns component-level confinement of a client-side AI model or runtime through Web Workers, sandboxed iframes, WASM capabilities, CSP, and minimal native bridges inside browsers, Electron shells, hybrid apps, or mobile runtimes. It does not own browser-agent task lifecycle or browser-managed and desktop-workspace state.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-007 isolates the embedded client-side model or runtime component; AID-I-008 isolates browser-agent and desktop computer-use state by task or trust zone.
Cookies, localStorage, IndexedDB, cache, history, downloads, clipboard, magic links, desktop profiles, and workspace residue belong to I-008 even when the model component is separately confined here.

AID-I-007 confines a model inside an end-user client application; AID-I-001 isolates managed AI execution in containers, sandboxes, or microVMs.
A client-side Worker or iframe boundary is not evidence that a server-side tool or model workload runs in the managed sandbox family.

AID-I-007 confines the client-side model runtime and its access to browser, application, operating-system, and native-bridge capabilities after execution begins; AID-H-003.011 decides whether an entitled, freshly attested client may receive the decryption key for an exact protected model release.
Client isolation does not authorize model delivery, and key-release admission does not prove post-release runtime confinement.

controls.name: Ephemeral Browser Context Lifecycle & Storage Partitioning
controls.description_text: Launch a fresh browser context for each task or trust zone, partition all browser-managed state surfaces (cookies, localStorage, IndexedDB, cache, history) by origin and trust set, and destroy the context deterministically when the task ends. This prevents browsing residue, authenticated sessions, and cached resources from leaking across tasks or being reused by unrelated origins.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns per-task or per-trust-zone browser-context creation, browser-managed cookie and storage partitioning, context rotation, and deterministic context teardown. It does not create the outer browser process sandbox or isolate non-browser agent memory.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-008.001 owns BrowserContext and browser-managed state lifecycle inside the runtime; AID-H-019.003 owns admission and launch of the outer browser runtime plus sanitized observation export.
Process isolation, blocked host profiles, and enforced egress do not prove per-task cookie or storage rotation, while a new BrowserContext does not establish the outer sandbox boundary.

AID-I-008.001 makes browser-profile state ephemeral per task or trust zone; AID-H-017.004 makes agent short-term prompt and session state transient and isolated.
The same lifecycle principle applies to different state owners, and neither control's cleanup receipt satisfies the other.

AID-I-008.001 isolates browser-engine state such as cookies, localStorage, IndexedDB, cache, and history; AID-I-004.001 isolates volatile model and agent working context.
Browser storage is not conversational context, and clearing one does not establish cleanup of the other.

controls.name: Cross-Origin Read/Write Segmentation with Step-Up Confirmation
controls.description_text: Separate browsing permissions by origin and effect type. Read-only origins may be inspected without authorization, but state-changing actions on sensitive or previously unseen origins must be suspended and bound to exact browser/request observations before execution.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the browser-specific observation and enforcement adapter for sensitive or cross-origin writes: complete request interception, stable actionable-element observation, exact request and UI binding, suspension, post-approval re-observation, drift-triggered receipt revocation, and resumption of the same request. It does not create a second generic approval service.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-008.002 observes, suspends, rebinds, and resumes the exact browser action; AID-H-018.003 independently validates the high-impact action and issues the canonical approval receipt.
The browser adapter supplies the exact observed binding but must consume the canonical H-018 decision rather than authorizing the action itself.

AID-I-008.002 re-observes browser state and revokes the receipt on browser-specific drift; AID-H-018.006 owns generic execution-time authorization re-verification and anti-TOCTOU policy.
The browser adapter implements domain-specific evidence and suspension without replacing the canonical runtime authorization check.

AID-I-008.002 enforces the browser action gate; AID-D-015 detects missing, mismatched, expired, replayed, or bypassed approval evidence from independent telemetry.
The detector does not authorize or resume a request, and the enforcement adapter does not replace independent bypass monitoring.

controls.name: Download & Clipboard Transfer Quarantine
controls.description_text: Treat browser downloads and clipboard import or export as quarantine-required cross-boundary transfers. Downloads must not be opened until their complete bytes, type, scan evidence, and clean-context handoff satisfy policy; clipboard contents must not be silently reused across tasks, origins, tenants, or trust zones.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns quarantine, scan-evidence binding, clean-context handoff, and cross-task or cross-origin controls for browser downloads and clipboard import or export. It does not broker authentication-bearing navigation or decide general URL admission.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-008.003 quarantines downloaded bytes and clipboard transfers; AID-I-008.005 isolates magic links, OAuth callbacks, password resets, invitations, and other authentication-bearing navigation.
An authentication URL is not a file-transfer artifact, and download quarantine does not protect state, nonce, PKCE, one-time code, or redirect binding.

AID-I-008.003 governs files and clipboard content crossing out of or into the browser workspace; AID-H-019 governs URL admission, safe fetch, content demotion, and browser observation export.
Safe-fetch results can supply scan inputs, but this control owns the transfer quarantine and clean-context release decision.

controls.name: Desktop Computer-Use Workspace Isolation & Action Confirmation
controls.description_text: Run desktop GUI / OS-level computer-use agents inside disposable, task-scoped workspaces with logged-out defaults, screenshot redaction, independently reviewed screenshot-injection signals, OS automation allowlists, action-bound confirmation, post-action effect readback, and watch-mode kill switches. This prevents a model-controlled cursor or screen reader from silently acting on hidden UI instructions, stale logged-in sessions, local files, clipboard residue, password managers, device APIs, or enterprise applications outside the approved task scope.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns containment of desktop GUI and OS-level computer-use agents in disposable logged-out workspaces, privileged UI observation, screenshot-risk handling, OS automation allowlists, stable accessibility invocation, action-bound confirmation consumption, signed UI or API effect readback, watch-mode halt, and deterministic cleanup.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-008.004 isolates a complete desktop or VDI computer-use workspace; AID-I-008.001 isolates browser contexts and browser-managed storage inside a browser runtime.
Desktop files, applications, password managers, device APIs, and OS session residue require this broader workspace boundary.

AID-I-008.004 applies privileged desktop UI observation and invocation; AID-I-008.002 intercepts and binds sensitive browser requests and cross-origin writes.
A desktop click may not correspond to a browser request, while browser request suspension does not constrain other OS applications or device surfaces.

AID-I-008.004 contains the desktop workspace and its general clipboard boundary; AID-I-008.003 owns browser download and clipboard transfer quarantine and clean-context handoff.
Use the transfer control for moving bytes across the browser boundary and this control for the wider OS workspace and action surface.

AID-I-008.004 contains general desktop and UI automation; AID-I-008.005 brokers authentication-bearing browser navigation in a dedicated context.
A disposable desktop does not authorize exposing raw magic links, codes, tokens, or callback state to the model.

AID-I-008.004 binds and invokes the exact desktop UI action and reads back its effect; AID-H-018.003 independently validates the high-impact action and issues the canonical approval receipt.
The desktop adapter consumes that receipt and must not become a second approval authority.

AID-I-008.004 adds desktop-specific re-observation and effect evidence; AID-H-018.006 owns generic execution-time authorization re-verification and anti-TOCTOU policy.
Both checks remain necessary when screen state, target identity, or effective authority can change between approval and invocation.

AID-I-008.004 owns OS and desktop workspace containment; AID-H-019 owns URL admission, safe fetch, browser-content demotion, and sanitized observation export.
Safe web-content handling does not constrain local apps, files, screenshots, or accessibility actions outside the browser surface.

controls.name: Magic-Link & Authentication-Bearing Navigation Isolation
controls.description_text: Isolate magic links, OAuth authorization redirects and callbacks, password-reset, invitation, email-verification, and other authentication-bearing navigation as separate, brokered transitions. A trusted controller—not the model—must resolve each opaque link handle; verify issuer, audience or client, exact redirect, transaction binding, expiry, state and nonce, PKCE where applicable, and one-time replay state; restrict the dedicated context to signed allowlisted origins with no inherited storage, permissions, downloads, or clipboard; return only a scoped session reference; then destroy the context and verify the destruction receipt. Raw URLs, authorization codes, access or refresh tokens, and link secrets must never enter model context, ordinary logs, or evidence.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns brokered isolation of magic links, OAuth redirects and callbacks, password resets, invitations, email verification, and other authentication-bearing navigation in a dedicated context with issuer, audience, redirect, transaction, expiry, state, nonce, PKCE, replay, origin, and destruction checks. Raw links, codes, and tokens must not enter model context.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-I-008.005 brokers authentication-bearing navigation and returns only a scoped session reference; AID-I-008.003 quarantines browser downloads and clipboard transfers.
Treating a magic link as an ordinary download or clipboard item does not protect transaction binding, one-time replay state, redirect trust, or token secrecy.

AID-I-008.005 owns the dedicated authentication-navigation state machine; AID-H-019 owns general URL admission and safe fetch outside authentication transitions.
A URL that passes generic admission still requires brokered authentication checks when it carries or creates authority.

controls.name: Honeypot AI Services & Decoy Models/APIs
controls.description_text:
Deploy and isolate decoy AI systems such as fake LLM APIs, ML model endpoints serving synthetic or non-sensitive data, or imitation agent services that appear valuable, vulnerable, or legitimate to potential attackers; record every interaction without exposing production data or authority.

Intelligence Collection
These honeypots are instrumented for intensive monitoring to log all interactions, capture attacker TTPs (Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures), and gather threat intelligence without exposing real production systems or data. They can also be used to slow down attackers or waste their resources.

Operational Requirements
All honeypot services must be logically isolated from production networks, run with read-only/non-destructive behaviors, and be instrumented for forensic retention (full request capture, replayable context).

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns the isolated decoy AI service, its synthetic behavior, and the evidence generated by interactions with that service. It must not expose production data, authority, credentials, or a route to a real inference backend.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-DV-001 operates a complete decoy AI service; AID-DV-006 exposes narrow synthetic reconnaissance routes at a gateway or proxy.
Use AID-DV-001 when the attacker interacts with an imitation model, agent, or API service. Use AID-DV-006 when only selected metadata or diagnostic-looking routes are populated and intercepted upstream.

controls.name: Honey Data, Decoy Artifacts & Canary Tokens for AI
controls.description_text: Seed and monitor approved AI assets, including training datasets, model repositories, configuration files, and API documentation, with synthetic decoy records, non-functional or instrumented model artifacts, or non-authoritative canary tokens. Access, exfiltration, or attempted use must generate a uniquely attributable alert and evidence without granting production access or disclosing sensitive data.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns passive, pre-seeded honey records, decoy artifacts, fake credentials, and canary tokens placed in datasets, repositories, configuration, or documentation. They generate attributable evidence when accessed, copied, exported, or used, without requiring an agent to choose a decoy capability.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-DV-002 plants passive decoy material; AID-DV-005 presents active canary goals, tools, MCP servers, or sub-agents for agent invocation.
Choose the control according to the trigger: access or attempted use of a pre-seeded artifact belongs here, while selection or invocation of a decoy agent capability belongs to AID-DV-005.

AID-DV-002 detects interaction with pre-seeded honey material; AID-DV-004 emits exact output markers from controlled trap prompts and investigates marker reuse.
AID-DV-002 does not own output-triggered marker activation, external marker scanning, or leak-beacon correlation.

AID-DV-002 uses access-triggered operational decoys; AID-DV-007 inserts authorized training canaries and measures their behavior in an exact model version.
Training-run insertion provenance, blinded recall measurement, and statistical evidence belong to AID-DV-007 rather than this passive artifact control.

controls.name: Dynamic Response Manipulation for AI Interactions
controls.description_text: For a high-confidence malicious session that satisfies a versioned deception-eligibility policy, deliberately return a controlled low-utility, misleading, randomized, or safe-no-op response to frustrate extraction, injection, jailbreak, or tool-misuse attempts and collect additional intelligence.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns deception-response eligibility, bounded execution, telemetry, and deterministic return to the normal allow, block, or review path for a high-confidence malicious session. Never activate it from a single weak signal, for ordinary users, or in excluded policy-defined high-impact domains. It requires calibrated multi-signal eligibility, legal and product approval, internal tagging, bounded duration, explicit exit conditions, and an independently controlled deception-mode disable switch.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-DV-003 selects and serves a controlled deceptive response; AID-H-018 authorizes and constrains actual tool actions and side effects.
A deception response or safe no-op does not replace the canonical runtime authorization policy for a real tool or capability.

AID-DV-003 can disable deception mode; AID-I-005 halts or severely restricts the AI system or tenant.
The deception-mode switch returns traffic to the normal response path and must not be represented as a system-wide emergency halt.

controls.name: AI Output Telemetry Traps & Leak Beacons
controls.description_text:
Telemetry Traps
Design model or agent APIs to return unique, benign marker strings only for tightly controlled trap prompts, trap-only synthetic records, or synthetic probe workflows. A marker hit outside the trusted runtime is treated as evidence of scraping, model theft, unauthorized model replay, or enterprise data leakage.

Leak Beacons
Maintain a private registry of exact marker strings, trap identifiers, activation events, and investigation owners. Continuously scan relevant external surfaces and internal telemetry for exact marker reuse, then correlate hits with the original trap activation and access logs.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns controlled trap prompts, exact benign marker strings, leak beacons, activation telemetry, external marker scanning, and marker-hit investigation. A marker establishes correlation with the registered trap workflow; it does not by itself prove watermark provenance, dataset access, or unauthorized training.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-DV-004 registers and investigates exact deception markers; AID-H-013.001 embeds and verifies watermarks or signed content provenance.
A leak investigation may consume AID-H-013.001 detector results, but this technique does not own watermark embedding, C2PA provenance, or modality-specific watermark registries.

AID-DV-004 activates and tracks output markers; AID-DV-002 owns pre-seeded honey data, decoy artifacts, fake credentials, and access-triggered canary tokens.
Use AID-DV-004 for marker reuse observed after a controlled activation, and AID-DV-002 for interaction with a decoy item that already exists in an asset or repository.

AID-DV-004 investigates externally observed exact marker reuse; AID-DV-007 measures registered behavioral canaries in a controlled training or fine-tuning context.
AID-DV-004 consumes a DV-007 canary only when that canary is deliberately registered for external leak investigation; it does not own the training-run measurement.

controls.name: Decoy Agent Behaviors & Canary Tasks
controls.description_text: For autonomous AI agents, design and implement decoy or canary functionalities, goals, tools, MCP servers, or sub-agents that appear valuable or sensitive but are actually monitored traps. If an attacker manipulates an agent through prompt injection, memory poisoning, or tool misuse and causes it to invoke a canary goal or tool, the invocation triggers an alert without risking real assets.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns active deception surfaces intentionally exposed to autonomous agents, including canary goals, tools, MCP servers, and sub-agents that generate attributable evidence when selected or invoked. It does not own generic agent telemetry, transcript scanning, or anomaly detection that is unrelated to a registered canary surface.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-DV-005 detects invocation of an active decoy capability; AID-DV-002 detects access to or attempted use of passive pre-seeded honey material.
The distinction is the engineered trigger: agent selection or invocation belongs here, while access, copy, export, or use of an existing decoy artifact belongs to AID-DV-002.

AID-DV-005 owns the decoy agent capability and canary-specific alert; AID-D-005.004 owns general agent and session event capture.
Agent logging may carry the invocation evidence, but generic telemetry without a registered canary goal or tool is not this deception control.

controls.name: Synthetic System-Information Decoy Routes
controls.description_text: Expose and monitor narrowly scoped, explicitly isolated reconnaissance paths that return synthetic framework, version, topology, debug, or environment metadata and generate high-confidence interaction telemetry. The decoy route must not read production configuration, secrets, diagnostics, or model identity.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns gateway or proxy population, priority, interception, and non-fallback routing for narrow synthetic reconnaissance paths. It must never read or fall through to truthful production diagnostics, configuration, secrets, or model identity.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-DV-006 deliberately serves synthetic metadata on isolated trap routes; AID-H-032.003 minimizes or disables truthful inference telemetry and debug surfaces.
A production route that should disclose nothing belongs to AID-H-032.003. A separately isolated route intentionally populated with synthetic reconnaissance data belongs here.

AID-DV-006 implements selected synthetic reconnaissance routes; AID-DV-001 operates a full decoy model, agent, or AI API service.
Use this technique when a gateway or proxy can intercept a narrow path without exposing a broader imitation service.

controls.name: Training-Data Provenance & Behavioral Canaries
controls.description_text: Insert authorized, synthetic, non-sensitive behavioral canaries into a controlled training or fine-tuning corpus and later run a pre-registered, statistically powered recall audit against the exact model version. The control produces evidence that a measured model exhibits behavior associated with the registered canary set; it does not by itself prove who copied data, when training occurred, or that the surrounding corpus was stolen.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns authorized behavioral-canary design, insertion provenance, blinded measurement against the exact model and query profile, statistical evidence, and handoff. Its result associates measured behavior with the registered canary set; it does not prove who copied data, when training occurred, that the surrounding corpus was stolen, or that a training anomaly is poisoning.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-DV-007 inserts and measures training-specific behavioral canaries; AID-DV-002 owns operational honey records, decoy artifacts, fake credentials, and access-triggered tokens.
AID-DV-002 alerts on interaction with planted material, while this technique requires a registered training insertion and a statistically powered model-behavior audit.

AID-DV-007 produces training-bound behavioral-canary evidence; AID-DV-004 owns external exact-marker observation and leak investigation.
An externally observed marker is handled by AID-DV-004 only when the behavioral canary was deliberately registered for that investigation path.

AID-DV-007 measures registered canary behavior after authorized insertion; AID-H-007.002 monitors the integrity and behavior of the running training job.
Canary loss or gradient signals may support investigation, but training telemetry and poisoning detection do not become a provenance verdict under this technique.

controls.name: Root & Long-Lived Credential Object Eviction
controls.description_text: Revoke, disable, rotate, or invalidate the exact incident-scoped population of root and long-lived credential objects, including passwords, API keys, client secrets, signing keys, and long-lived certificates, at their authoritative issuer or verifier regardless of whether the owning principal is a human, conventional service, AI agent, or workload.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns incident-time revocation, disablement, rotation, or invalidation of the exact root and long-lived credential-object population, including passwords, API keys, client secrets, signing keys, and long-lived certificates. Routine non-incident secret rotation is outside this control.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-E-001.001 evicts root and long-lived credential objects; AID-E-001.002 revokes already-issued tokens, authentication sessions, cookies, certificates, and leases.
Rotating a root secret does not prove that every artifact already issued from it is unusable, so both controls may be required for the same incident.

AID-E-001.001 evicts individual long-lived credentials; AID-E-001.003 disables the AI-agent or workload principal and its ability to obtain new credentials.
A principal can retain other issuance paths after one secret is rotated, while disabling the principal does not independently rotate every exposed credential object.

AID-E-001.001 evicts credential objects; AID-E-001.004 removes delegated grants and connected-app authorizations.
A grant can sustain or recreate access after credential rotation, and grant revocation does not invalidate an unrelated password, key, secret, or certificate.

controls.name: Issued Token, Authentication Session & Lease Revocation
controls.description_text: Revoke or invalidate the complete incident-scoped population of already-issued access tokens, refresh tokens, session cookies, authorization-server sessions, gateway authentication sessions, and agent-to-agent leases at every authoritative issuer, verifier, cache, and enforcement point.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns revocation or invalidation of the complete incident-scoped population of already-issued access and refresh tokens, session cookies, authorization-server sessions, gateway authentication sessions, workload certificates, established authenticated channels, and agent-to-agent leases. Automated response integration is only an implementation method, not a separate control outcome.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-E-001.002 revokes already-issued authentication artifacts; AID-E-001.001 evicts their root or long-lived credential objects.
Revoking current tokens and sessions does not rotate a compromised password, key, client secret, signing key, or long-lived certificate that can issue future artifacts.

AID-E-001.002 invalidates artifacts already issued to a principal; AID-E-001.003 disables the principal and stops new issuance.
Existing tokens can remain effective after principal disablement, and revoking the current token set does not necessarily prevent the principal from obtaining replacements.

AID-E-001.002 revokes issued tokens and authentication sessions; AID-E-001.004 removes the delegated grants or connected-app authorizations that can mint fresh tokens or sustain SaaS access.
Both populations require authoritative verification when a delegated authorization was involved.

AID-E-001.002 revokes identity-provider and gateway authentication sessions; AID-E-005 removes durable application session and agent-state records.
A durable conversation, webhook, queue, schedule, or tool registration can survive authentication-session revocation and reload compromised state later.

controls.name: AI Agent & Workload Principal and Issuance Disablement
controls.description_text:
Disable the exact compromised AI-agent or workload principal at every authoritative identity, workload, federation, and authorization control plane, and stop that principal from obtaining newly issued credentials or tokens. Applicable principal and issuance objects include agent identities, workload or service-principal records, SPIFFE workload entries, cloud workload-identity bindings, provider-native agent identities, and token-exchange or on-behalf-of issuance permissions.

Eviction sequence:

1. Disable the principal and stop new issuance or delegated minting.
2. Deny the principal at every reachable authorization and federation boundary.
3. Invalidate or deny every applicable fresh-authentication and issuance path.
4. Register a separately attested replacement principal under least privilege when recovery requires one.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns disablement of the exact compromised AI-agent or workload principal at every authoritative identity, workload, federation, and authorization plane and denial of every fresh credential or token issuance path. A separately attested replacement principal is a recovery object, not proof that the original principal was disabled.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-E-001.003 disables the principal and stops new issuance; AID-E-001.001 revokes or rotates individual root and long-lived credential objects.
Principal disablement does not independently rotate every exposed password, key, secret, signing key, or certificate.

AID-E-001.003 stops the principal from obtaining new authentication artifacts; AID-E-001.002 revokes tokens, sessions, certificates, and leases that were already issued.
An issuer-side disablement does not prove that every relying party rejects previously issued artifacts.

AID-E-001.003 disables an AI-agent or workload principal and its issuance paths; AID-E-001.004 removes delegated grants and connected-app authorizations.
Delegated authorization can remain independently effective or associated with another principal, so its authoritative grant population requires separate eviction.

controls.name: Delegated Grant & Connected-App Authorization Revocation
controls.description_text: Revoke the complete incident-scoped population of delegated OAuth grants, connected-app consents, service-principal app-role assignments, token-exchange or on-behalf-of delegated authorizations, and SaaS application grants that can mint fresh tokens or sustain access after ordinary token invalidation.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns incident-time revocation of delegated OAuth grants, connected-app consents, app-role assignments, token-exchange or on-behalf-of authorizations, and SaaS application grants that can mint fresh tokens or sustain access. It does not own credential, token, principal, application-state, or pre-incident authorization design.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-E-001.004 removes delegated authorization objects; AID-E-001.001 evicts root and long-lived credentials.
Grant revocation does not rotate an exposed password, key, client secret, signing key, or certificate, and credential rotation does not necessarily remove an independent connected-app consent.

AID-E-001.004 removes authorization that can sustain or recreate access; AID-E-001.002 revokes tokens and authentication sessions already issued under that authority.
Both controls are required when issued artifacts remain valid after the underlying grant is removed.

AID-E-001.004 revokes delegated grants and app authorizations; AID-E-001.003 disables the compromised AI-agent or workload principal and stops new principal issuance.
Removing one grant does not disable the principal's other authorization paths, while principal disablement does not prove removal of every connected-app or delegated grant object.

AID-E-001.004 performs incident-time removal of delegated grant objects; AID-H-034.002 enforces MCP server OAuth resource boundaries and delegation safety before compromise.
Preventive OAuth design does not revoke a compromised live grant, and grant eviction does not replace correct protected-resource and audience enforcement.

AID-E-001.004 removes authorization grants; AID-E-005 deletes rogue webhook, tool-registration, queue, schedule, and durable application-state records.
Revoke the grant before or alongside teardown, but do not treat removal of either population as proof that the other is gone.

controls.name: AI Runtime Process, Lease & Pod Eviction
controls.description_text: Revoke compromised execution leases and terminate confirmed-compromised AI model processes, agent runs, supervisor jobs, pods, or containerized runtime instances so active malicious execution stops and cannot reacquire work.

scope_boundary.responsibility: Owns revocation of active execution leases and termination of confirmed-compromised processes, agent runs, supervisor jobs, pods, containers, and run-local ephemeral execution. It does not remove the credentials, durable application state, or deployable artifacts that could recreate execution.

related_techniques.comparison:
AID-E-002 terminates active execution; AID-E-001 revokes the credentials, sessions, principals, and grants that authorize execution.
A killed process can restart while authority remains, and revoked authority does not prove that the currently running workload stopped.

AID-E-002 terminates active workers, processes, runs, jobs, pods, and containers; AID-E-005 removes durable application session, memory, registration, queue, and schedule records.
